articles.title: How Travis Kelce expanded beyond football with 13 investments, a $200M beer brand and ownership in his hometown team
articles.summary: Travis Kelce now has money in a beer company valued at about $200 million, a theme park giant, a mattress maker and his hometown baseball team.
articles.body: Travis Kelce now has money in a beer company valued at about $200 million, a theme park giant, a mattress maker and his hometown baseball team. The Chiefs tight end announced a minority stake in the Cleveland Guardians on May 27, adding to a list that already included Six Flags, Sleep Number and Alpine F1. Garage Beer, which he co-owns with his brother Jason, has been available at every U.S. Red Robin since July 21. None of it depends on his next catch. His 2026 Chiefs deal is reportedly a one-year contract.How did Travis Kelce expand beyond football with so many investments?The portfolio grew in layers. A CB Insights profile from early 2025 listed 12 investments and one exit, Cholula in 2020. The biggest deals have come fast since then. In October 2025, he joined activist firm Jana Partners and other investors in a group that holds about 9% of Six Flags, a stake The Wall Street Journal valued near $200 million. That figure covers the whole group, not Kelce alone. He calls himself a "lifelong Six Flags fan," and the timing was bold, since the company's shares fell more than 45% in 2025.Sleep Number followed in January. Kelce took a stake of under 5% and signed on for three years of national ads. He bought some shares himself and will receive restricted stock that vests over those three years. In March, Tommy Hilfiger named him a global brand ambassador in a multi-season deal. Fox 4 Kansas City also lists a stake in an Alpine Formula 1 team, an arena football team, a car wash company and the Kansas City steakhouse 1587 Prime.How much is Garage Beer worth, and does Travis Kelce own all of it?No. Garage Beer has several owners. Travis and Jason joined in June 2024 as co-owners and operators. In September 2025, private equity firm Durational Capital Management put money into the brand's first outside funding round, and The Wall Street Journal reported a valuation of roughly $200 million. CEO Andy Sauer said revenue was on track for $60 million to $70 million that year, up from under $20 million in 2024. Kelce's personal share has not been made public, so $200 million is the company's value, not his.The brand sells two beers, Classic Light and Lime. Both carry 4% alcohol and 95 calories. The Red Robin rollout makes the chain the first national restaurant group to serve Garage Beer in every U.S. location, which puts the product in front of diners and not only in coolers.Why did Travis Kelce buy into the Cleveland Guardians?Home, mostly. Kelce grew up in Cleveland Heights and played baseball at Cleveland Heights High School, where his father Ed coached him. The Guardians announced his minority purchase on May 27, and he called it a "dream come true for a Cleveland kid." The price and the size of his stake were not disclosed.One detail gives the deal extra weight. Partner David Blitzer can become the controlling owner after the 2027 season, or wait and use that option later. Kelce has bought into a group that could change leadership soon.Put the pieces side by side and the pattern is hard to miss. A beer brand, a theme park chain, a mattress company and a ballclub all pay off whether or not he keeps playing. He has never confirmed retirement plans. articles.body: Ciara is once again giving fans plenty to talk about, not just because of her growing baby bump, but also because of the eye-catching diamond ring she recently showed off. The singer, who is expecting her fifth child and fourth with husband Russell Wilson, appeared in a stunning black lace maternity look while proudly displaying her pregnancy bump. But eagle-eyed fans quickly focused on the enormous ring on her finger.Ciara’s jaw-dropping ring sparks fan theory that Russell Wilson added a diamond for every babyOne fan reposted the footage and wrote, “My goodness what is that ring?? Russell put a new diamond on it for each new baby?? WOW.” The theory quickly caught attention online, with fans wondering whether Wilson has been adding diamonds to Ciara’s ring as their family has grown.The couple announced in September that they are expecting another child, with Ciara showing off her growing bump in a creative pregnancy reveal. Their announcement featured four shirts representing their existing children and a blank baby onesie for the newest addition. They captioned the post, “One more person to Love.”Ciara and Wilson are already parents to Sienna Princess, Win Harrison, and Amora Princess. Ciara also shares her eldest son, Future Zahir, with rapper Future. The upcoming arrival will be her fifth child and her fourth with Wilson. The pregnancy also fulfills Wilson’s long-running desire for another child. He had previously joked about wanting a fifth baby and even referred to the hoped-for addition as “Cinco.”But did Russell really add a diamond for every baby?That is where the viral fan theory gets interesting. There is no confirmed report or public statement from Ciara, Wilson or the jeweler establishing that Wilson adds a new diamond to her ring for every child. So while fans are speculating about the meaning behind the ring, the “one diamond for each baby” explanation should not be presented as a confirmed tradition.What is documented is that Wilson proposed to Ciara in 2016 with a spectacular diamond engagement ring, which has long been one of the standout pieces in her jewelry collection. Current celebrity-ring coverage continues to highlight the size and extravagance of the piece. That has not stopped fans from connecting the dots as Ciara prepares to become a mother of five. articles.title: How Patrick Mahomes uses 30+ Whataburger locations and 4 team stakes to build an off-field empire beyond his $450 million deal
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes signed a 10-year, $450 million extension with the Chiefs in 2020, and he has spent the years since turning part of that income into
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes signed a 10-year, $450 million extension with the Chiefs in 2020, and he has spent the years since turning part of that income into ownership. He holds stakes in four sports teams and sits inside KMO Burger, the group that operates 29 Whataburger restaurants across Kansas and Missouri and has aimed for 30 since day one. In June 2026, the Chiefs reworked his contract again, lifting it to $504.75 million through 2033, according to the Associated Press. The paycheck is the headline, but the stakes are where his long game sits.How does Patrick Mahomes build an off-field empire beyond his $450 million deal?Start with the paycheck, because it explains everything else. When Mahomes signed in July 2020, the headline number was $503 million. The base deal was $450 million over 10 years. The rest came from incentives and the last two years of his rookie contract. It was the richest contract in sports at the time, and it left one obvious question. What happens to a player whose income rides on a single left knee?Last December gave a blunt answer. Mahomes tore the ACL and LCL in that knee against the Chargers on Dec. 14, had surgery the next day and missed the last three games of a 6-11 season. He was back at practice by late May and was cleared without restrictions for the opener, according to reports. In June, the Chiefs reworked the deal again. The new version runs through 2033 at $504.75 million, with escalators that could lift it to $522.25 million, the AP reported. That averages $63.1 million a year.A salary depends on a healthy quarterback. A stake in a team or a restaurant group keeps working when he is on the sideline. That is the quiet logic behind every move below.How many Whataburger restaurants is Mahomes tied to?The story starts with ketchup. In 2018, Mahomes made his love for the brand public, and when Whataburger tweeted him a picture of its sauce and asked where to ship it, he wrote back, "I just want a store in Kansas City!"Three years later, it became a business. In August 2021, Whataburger announced KMO Burger, an investor-led franchise group that included Mahomes, with a plan for 30 restaurants from Wichita, Kansas, to St. Joseph, Missouri, over seven years. "I love Kansas City and I love Whataburger," Mahomes said at the time. The first KMO restaurant opened on June 7, 2022, on Parallel Parkway in Kansas City, Kansas, with a Mahomes jersey and a plaque for his No. 15 inside.The real jump came in May 2025. Whataburger put its 16 company-owned restaurants in the Kansas City and Springfield, Missouri, markets into a joint venture with KMO, which brought 13 of its own. KMO now operates all 29. "Our team at KMO Burger is ready to keep raising the bar," Mahomes said. Terms were not disclosed, so nobody outside the deal knows what his piece is worth. The chain itself had more than 1,100 restaurants in 16 states at that point, which makes this a regional franchise group, not a takeover of the brand.Which four teams does Mahomes own a piece of?The Royals came first. He bought into the Kansas City baseball club in July 2020, weeks after signing the extension, as a minority owner. A year later, on July 27, 2021, he joined the ownership group of Sporting Kansas City. ESPN reported that he had already attended at least 12 matches by then and had even led fans in a chant at Children's Mercy Park.The next two came close together. In December 2022, he joined the group behind the Miami Pickleball Club in Major League Pickleball, alongside Naomi Osaka, Nick Kyrgios and agent Rich Paul. Forbes reported that expansion fees for comparable teams ran from $1 million to $3 million. Then, on Jan. 10, 2023, he joined his wife, Brittany, as an owner of the Kansas City Current in the NWSL. The club said he was the first active NFL player with equity in a team in that league.Put together, the list reads like a map of his interests: baseball, soccer, women's sports and a fast-growing paddle game.Why does Mahomes keep investing in Kansas City first?Three of the four teams sit in one metro area, and so do most of the burger restaurants. That is not an accident. In a mid-sized market, a face that fans trust can move a team's brand more than the same face would in New York or Los Angeles. The quarterback gets equity that grows with the city, and the city gets a hometown name behind its clubs.The Whataburger deal is the most telling piece, mostly because it is the least glamorous. A drive-thru that stays open around the clock is a daily, repeatable business. KMO also backs charities such as Make-A-Wish and Special Olympics through Mahomes' foundation, Franchise Times reported, so the restaurants carry some community weight too.None of it is risk-free. Minority stakes give little say over decisions, restaurant margins run thin, and a young pickleball league has not yet proved it will last. What keeps the mix sensible is scale. A $1 million to $3 million team buy-in is a small slice next to a $450 million deal.Can Mahomes own an NFL team one day?He says that is the goal. In 2023, when he joined an ownership group in Formula 1, Mahomes talked about owning an NFL team once he retires and noted that Tom Brady was already working on it. "That's definitely where you want to get to," he said, as ESPN relayed.The Chiefs now hold his contract through 2033, when he will be 38. Between now and then, the Whataburger group, the four teams and the Formula 1 stake read like a long application for a seat in the owners' box.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "It was weird": Mike Vrabel and Dianna Russini controversy gets fresh twist from ex-Raiders star
articles.summary: Former Las Vegas Raiders star Richie Incognito has brought a 2019 memory back into the spotlight amid renewed interest in the controversy surrounding Mike
articles.body: Former Las Vegas Raiders star Richie Incognito has brought a 2019 memory back into the spotlight amid renewed interest in the controversy surrounding Mike Vrabel and Dianna Russini. Incognito recalled meeting Vrabel at a Super Bowl party in Miami and said the then-Tennessee Titans coach introduced him to Russini during their conversation. The retired NFL offensive lineman admitted that the introduction struck him as unusual at the time, adding another detail to a story that has attracted major attention around the NFL.Richie Incognito recalls Mike Vrabel and Dianna Russini meetingIncognito shared the story during Saturday's episode of the Initial Contact show. He was discussing a Super Bowl party hosted by NFL insider Jay Glazer after the 2019 season when he remembered running into Vrabel.The former Raiders lineman said the two first spoke about their teams' meeting that season. Oakland had faced Tennessee, and Incognito recalled Vrabel praising the Raiders' offensive line.He then described how the conversation shifted when Vrabel introduced him to Russini."I got a good Vrabel-Russini story," Incognito said. "It's after the 2019 season. We're down in Miami and it's a Super Bowl party. Jay Glazer throws this great Super Bowl party at like this auto collection place. There's all these exotic cars, and the Oakland Raiders have played the Tennessee Titans that year.""So I see Vrabel at the party, and I go up, and I'm like, 'Hey Vrabes, you guys were tough. We should have won that game.' He's like, 'Listen, you guys were some dudes. That's the biggest offensive line we've ever faced. I told my guys they had to be ready. You guys brought it.' So me and Vrabel are having this conversation, and mid-conversation, he goes, 'Oh, let me introduce you to Dianna Russini.' And I go, 'Oh, hey, what's up, Dianna? How you doing?' And I always thought it was weird."Incognito's account is a recollection of an encounter from several years ago. His comment about finding the introduction unusual reflects his own reaction at the time and does not, by itself, establish anything beyond the meeting he described.Mike Vrabel and Dianna Russini controversy returns to NFL spotlightThe story has resurfaced after photos involving Vrabel and Russini from previous years triggered widespread online speculation during the offseason. The controversy eventually became a major talking point across NFL media.Russini later resigned from her position at The Athletic. Vrabel, meanwhile, remains focused on his coaching career and is in his second season with the New England Patriots.The Patriots entered Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills with a 1-2 record after three games. articles.title: Bills' C.J. Gardner-Johnson on Efton Chism's game-winning TD: 'Probably won't hear from him again'
articles.summary: Efton Chism made a terrific TD catch to help the Patriots win in Buffalo, but the Bills' safety was unimpressed.
articles.body:
Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson said he didn't want to get into any "bulletin-board material" after Buffalo's 29-26 loss to the New England Patriots.

Then CJGJ took shots at the Patriots and Efton Chism, who caught the go-ahead touchdown.

Chism caught two passes, both on the go-ahead drive: a 19-yard grab and, three plays later, the catch of his football life. He made a one-handed stab of Drake Maye's pass and hauled it in, despite coverage blanketed all over Chism.

Chism made the most of his opportunity after Mack Hollins' injury, playing a season-high 34 snaps on offense and hauling in only his second career TD. The Patriots held on for a massive, perhaps season-shifting victory.

Watch Mike Vrabel's greeting of Chism after the game:

Consider Gardner-Johnson relatively unimpressed.

"Elevated guy made a hell of a catch," Gardner-Johnson said of Chism, even though he was not elevated from the Patriots' practice squad. He's been on New England's 53-man roster since August cutdowns.

Gardner-Johnson seemed to be speaking more of Chism's relative anonymity outside of New England, suggesting this might be Chism's career high-water mark.

"Probably won't hear from him again, respectfully," Gardner-Johnson added. "I say that with a lot of confidence."

Naturally, Chism was more upbeat postgame, grinning through his entire answer about the final catch.

"When I am out there, and the ball's in the air, I kind of black out," he said. "I am kind of in that little flow state. I saw it in the air, Drake gave me that opportunity, and I just … you gotta take advantage of those opportunities, you never know when they're gonna come."

In Gardner-Johnson's mind, Chism might not have too many more opportunities. CJGJ admitted the Bills blew their opportunity Sunday, even if giving the Patriots credit for the win was a bridge too far for him.

"They won the game, whatever," Gardner-Johnson said. "They didn't do s*** better than us. We gotta play better."

articles.title: Russell Wilson and Ciara donate $250,000 as Spokane families face the aftermath of historic wildfires
articles.summary: Russell Wilson and Ciara are stepping in to help Spokane families facing the long road back after a devastating wildfire season.
articles.body: Russell Wilson and Ciara are stepping in to help Spokane families facing the long road back after a devastating wildfire season. Their Why Not You Foundation has committed $250,000 to The Salvation Army of Spokane, with the money aimed at both urgent relief and longer-term support. The donation comes as communities continue dealing with destroyed homes, evacuations, financial pressure and disrupted services. Rather than limiting the gift to emergency response, the foundation’s contribution will also help families access food, child care, education and other essential programmes in the months ahead.Russell Wilson and Ciara donate $250,000 to Spokane familiesThe $250,000 donation arrives as Spokane County and other parts of Eastern Washington work through the damage left by the 2026 wildfires. The Salvation Army will use the funding to respond to families affected by the fires while continuing services for people facing hardship throughout the year.Captain David Cain, director of The Salvation Army of Spokane, said the contribution gives the organisation room to respond to changing needs.“This gift allows us to respond to families who have been impacted by the wildfires while also ensuring that families who are struggling can access support throughout the year,” Cain said.The money will support several programmes, including the Hope Market Food Bank and Family Resource Center, After the Bell after-school services, and back-to-school, summer camp and Christmas assistance.It will also help Sally’s House and Evangeline’s House, which provide emergency foster care for children arriving from unsafe or abusive homes.That wider reach matters because recovery does not end when evacuation orders are lifted. Families can face new costs long after a fire has passed, from replacing essentials to finding stable care and getting children back into normal routines.Spokane wildfire recovery gets support from Russell Wilson and CiaraThe scale of the disaster underlines why donations such as the Wilsons’ are important. A preliminary assessment found that the fires destroyed 649 primary residences, damaged another 2,542 homes and burned nearly 369,000 acres across affected areas.Spokane County suffered some of the heaviest losses. More than 65,000 people were evacuated, while hundreds of homes were destroyed or damaged. Essential services, healthcare and utilities were also disrupted.Cain stressed that the foundation's investment can reach families dealing with very different challenges.“Whether a family has lost something because of a wildfire, is struggling to put food on the table, is worried about sending their children back to school, or simply needs a little help getting through the holidays, this investment will make a tangible difference” Cain said.The donation therefore extends beyond immediate wildfire relief. It gives The Salvation Army additional resources to keep helping families as Spokane moves from emergency response toward rebuilding and recovery.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 4 Booms and Busts: Comeback kids Nico Collins, Drake Maye return to form
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Scott Pianowski examines Sunday's winners and losers in Week 4.
articles.body:
We often talk of the NFL being a snow globe league. If you don't like what you're seeing, wait a week, or an hour, or even a play. Comebacks are an eternal part of the NFL story. And we had plenty to choose from in Week 4.

Let's start with Puka Nacua, who made his first start since Week 1. He threw a classic Nacua line at the Eagles (9-125-0, plus a rushing touchdown), helping the Rams overcome a 10-point deficit and improve to 2-2 . Perhaps the game never really should have been close, because Los Angeles dominated the stats; the Rams had 415 yards of offense, the Eagles just 172. Nonetheless, it's fun to have Nacua back to set-and-forget status.

Davante Adams (4-32-0, nine targets) didn't run with Nacua on this day, though Matthew Stafford missed him on one long pass. The surprising second pitch for the Rams has been Kyren Williams (147 total yards, two scores), who's stepped up as a receiver this year. After catching between 32 and 36 passes for three straight seasons, Williams has 16 receptions over the last two weeks (10 on Sunday). Williams has turned the presumed LAR backfield rotation into a one-man show; Blake Corum has just 12 touches the last two games.

The Texans also welcomed their signature receiver back, though it wasn't enough to secure a critical win . Nico Collins was unstoppable against the Cowboys (7-118-2), with just one of his targets falling incomplete. Collins has missed time in each of his six pro seasons, so maintenance comes standard whenever you draft him. But when healthy, he's easily a top-10 fantasy receiver, with a case to push into the top five.

Collins somehow wasn't even the best fantasy wideout on the field Sunday, as CeeDee Lamb went ballistic on the other side (17-189-1), one of the best games of the year . Lamb collected 21 targets compared to just three for George Pickens, although Pickens did draw a couple of key penalty flags. Obviously the split in Dallas is going to move closer together in future weeks, but Lamb is making it clear who's the Batman and who's the Robin in this passing game. And maybe it's time we stopped worrying about when our fantasy players go up against the Houston defense — something is definitely missing with the Texans this year.

Perhaps no NFL player needed a Week 4 win as badly as Drake Maye, who was the most diagnosed and analyzed player of the week. Maye orchestrated an inspiring upset win at Buffalo , throwing for 269 yards and three touchdowns and resourcefully rushing for 54 more yards. Add in a 2-point conversion toss and Maye is the week's QB1 with two games left to go, scoring over 27 points. There's still stuff to iron out — three fumbles (one lost), one interception — but this was a massive step forward.

Maye was able to MacGyver this win with a skeleton crew on offense. Obviously, A.J. Brown is out indefinitely and glue-guy Mack Hollins was hurt Sunday. The game-winning touchdown came on a pretty Maye throw to Efton Chism, who made a dynamite one-handed catch . Romeo Doubs (6-58-2, nine targets) caught the other two scores from Maye, pushing into the flex mix moving forward.

The New England schedule softens up some over the second quarter. The team will be up against the Raiders, Jets, Bears and Dolphins the next four weeks. Some respectable matchups in there, but it's not like playing the Seahawks, Jaguars and Bills.

Speaking of welcome comebacks, let's celebrate the return of Jameis Winston being aggressive. After a buttoned-up Winston led the Giants to a conservative win last week, he was back to riverboat-gambler Winston in the Sunday win over Arizona. Winston threw two picks, took four sacks and pushed the ball downfield. He finished with 250 yards and three touchdowns as the Giants held off the Cardinals.

Most fantasy managers are tracking Winston's play only for how it affects his main targets. Sunday, business was good. Malik Nabers (6-112-1) cracked double-digit points for the first time in 2026, overcoming a dinged-up shoulder in the first half. And Winston looked liberally for tight end Isaiah Likely (7-66-0), sending 12 targets his way. The Giants should continue to be aggressive next week against a leaky Washington pass defense.

Every NFL Sunday is going to have the stench of injuries, and the Eagles feel that as much as anyone. Philadelphia started the day without DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert, and Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was hurt in the first half . The depleted Eagles never found an offensive rhythm, going 0-for-12 on first down and sputtering to 172 yards.

Jacksonville will be a challenge for the Eagles next week, no matter who Philly has available in the huddle. Jalen Hurts had just 93 passing yards against the Rams, and his two touchdowns were fantasy shockers, going to unheralded receiver Darius Cooper. Trendy sleepers Makai Lemon (3-27-0) and Dontayvion Wicks (3-18-0) failed to launch.

The Baltimore win over Tennessee was mostly a color-by-numbers job, a case of efficiency over flash. But part of that was mandatory after Lamar Jackson hurt his ankle in the first half. Backup QB Tyler Huntley played the second half and was only asked to throw nine passes (63 yards). The Ravens knew a Tennessee comeback was unlikely.

Zay Flowers (8-118-1) was electric with Jackson and could be one of the ADP smashes of the year if Jackson can get back on the field quickly. Of course, Flowers did produce with Huntley last year, too, but the upside would surely be capped with a backup QB. The Ravens travel to Atlanta for next Sunday night's game.

Ja'Marr Chase was another casualty in Week 4, suffering a first-half concussion against the Jaguars. Tee Higgins (11-157-0) became the target hog with Chase out, but he suffered an adductor injury on the final drive. There's a lot of Cincinnati stuff to unpack before they play at Miami next week. The Bengals then have a Week 6 bye.

Kyle Monangai (30-146-2) looked like the better of the two Chicago backs, though he suffered a thumb injury at some point in the win over the Jets. We also have to consider that D'Andre Swift (15-58-0) was playing with a sore knee. The Chicago passing game was more traditional with Tyson Bagent at the controls; Rome Odunze (6-94-0), Luther Burden III (4-63-0) and Colston Loveland (6-57-0) soaked up 22 of the 31 targets. But perhaps the biggest shock of all was the Chicago defense — feared to be a sieve a few weeks ago — holding the Jets to seven first downs and 157 yards of offense.

Maybe Chicago isn't the carnival team we all dreamt about. A trip to Green Bay is up next.

The Packers offense continued its early-season theme — bad running, ordinary passing. Of course, not much was needed against a Tampa Bay offense that was mostly punchless without Baker Mayfield. The best sign for Green Bay was Tucker Kraft (6-42-1) finding the end zone and drawing a team-high seven targets. Kraft has some fun matchups coming soon, especially Dallas in Week 6 and Detroit in Week 7.

A lot of words were spilled on the Dalton Kincaid breakout through two weeks (my keyboard was busy, too). But Kincaid has been erased since, with just 3-45-0 the last two games. The Patriots held him to two targets and just one catch Sunday, especially disappointing with DJ Moore (shoulder) leaving the game early. Josh Allen's best work came when targeting intriguing post-hype sleeper Keon Coleman (6-116-1) and slot man Khalil Shakir (7-82-0).

Although the Cardinals put up 24 points in the Meadowlands, the return wasn't that much fun for fantasy players. Arizona had a modest 270 yards of offense and the touchdowns went to players unlikely to be started in most leagues — Tyler Allgeier, Elijah Higgins, and yes, Marvin Harrison Jr. (his only catch).

Michael Wilson (7-95-0) and Trey McBride (7-31-0) weren't total washouts, but it was disappointing to see Jacoby Brissett struggle against the New York defense (three picks, two sacks, 4.7 YPA). The Cardinals have now lost three straight, and perhaps the Carson Beck experiment at quarterback will start sooner than expected.

No one wants to pile on Jalon Daniels — he was an undrafted rookie making his first NFL start. You're set up to fail in this type of spot. No one in the Tampa Bay huddle got past 40 yards receiving, and Daniels was held to 5.5 YPA. He also took three sacks, had two passes intercepted.

It was also a nightmare day for Bucky Irving managers — while 16-61-0 is respectable on the ground, he was not used in the passing game. Meanwhile, Sean Tucker had a short touchdown run and Kenny Gainwell had a touchdown catch. The Buccaneers need to find answers quickly; they travel to Dallas for a Thursday night game.

articles.title: $30 billion sports giant could turn Travis Kelce’s post-NFL chapter into a major media career
articles.summary: Travis Kelce may have another major stage waiting for him whenever his NFL career finally comes to an end.
articles.body: Travis Kelce may have another major stage waiting for him whenever his NFL career finally comes to an end. The Kansas City Chiefs star has already shown that his appeal extends well beyond the football field, and ESPN could be among the networks interested in that star power. For now, though, Kelce is firmly focused on playing. His strong start to the 2026 season has only added to the uncertainty over when he might walk away.Travis Kelce's ESPN opportunity could grow after retirementKelce's television future is attracting attention because he has already proved he can handle a microphone. His connection with ESPN also has an interesting link through Joe Buck, who continues to call Monday Night Football with Troy Aikman.Buck signed a six-year extension with ESPN in September 2026. The network is also preparing to broadcast Super Bowl LXI in February 2027. That gives ESPN a strong platform for former players who can bring both football knowledge and personality to its coverage.Still, there is no deal between Kelce and ESPN. Any suggestion that he is joining the network remains speculation until the Chiefs star announces his retirement and chooses his next career move.Travis Kelce's media experience gives him an edgeKelce would not enter broadcasting as a complete newcomer. He hosted Saturday Night Live in 2023 and later became the host of Prime Video's Are You Smarter Than a Celebrity? He also co-hosts New Heights with his brother Jason Kelce, giving him years of experience speaking freely about football, sports culture and entertainment.Jason's own move into broadcasting could make the transition even more natural. After retiring from the Philadelphia Eagles, he joined ESPN as an analyst on Monday Night Countdown in 2024. Travis has watched that path unfold while building his own media profile.His playing career also gives him plenty to discuss. Kelce entered the 2026 season with three Super Bowl titles, seven All-Pro selections and more than 13,000 receiving yards. More importantly, his recent form suggests retirement may still be some distance away.Through three games this season, Kelce had 14 catches for 231 yards and two touchdowns. He led the Chiefs in all three receiving categories while helping Kansas City open the campaign 3-0.So, while ESPN could eventually be an appealing destination, Kelce has little reason to rush into the next chapter. articles.title: 5 momentous plays: Nick Sirianni's field-goal decision, plus Kamari Lassiter's painful penalties
articles.summary: Here are some of the bigger but less-than-obvious momentum shifters in Sunday's games.
articles.body:
Week 4 wasn't quite the closely contested affair that Week 3 was , but there still were several one-score games that were decided by a handful of key plays.

A few were bad luck. Some of the close games came down to a handful of plays. But there were some below-the-radar moments in several of the tight ones that shifted the tides.

Here are some of the bigger but less-than-obvious momentum shifters in Sunday's games:

1. Kamari Lassiter's nightmare drive haunts Texans

Midway through the third quarter, the Texans led the Cowboys 23-13, and had Dallas in a third-and-7 at the Houston 8-yard line. It appeared Houston got a stop, but Texans cornerback Kamari Lassiter — who allowed a 53-yard catch earlier on the drive — was flagged for a back-breaking pass interference call.

Houston held firm the next three plays, moving the Cowboys back two yards. But on fourth-and-goal from the 3-yard line, Lassiter again was flagged, this time for holding. Houston couldn't hold again, as Javonte Williams' TD cut the Texans' lead to three.

That series completely flipped the game, one Dallas stormed back to win in the final minute .

The Texans were actually on the right side of a few big momentum plays before and after this. They blocked a field-goal try near the end of the first half, kicking their own FG for a six-point swing in a 30-second span. They also converted a third-and-14 hook-and-ladder play for 21 yards, setting up Houston's go-ahead TD with 2:26 remaining in the game.

But not getting that goal-line stop potentially cost them four points … in a four-point loss.

Lassiter is a talented, young player, but he and the Texans are in a dark place right now at 0-4.

The most controversial momentum swing came when Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni opted to go for it on fourth-and-goal from the 2, instead of kicking a field goal, leading 20-10 with 7:26 remaining against the visiting Rams. Jalen Hurts' pass was incomplete, and the Eagles got zero points out of the drive.

Perhaps trying to go for the kill shot there wasn't the worst idea in an effort to make it a three-possession game. A field goal would have given the Eagles a 13-point lead, but the Rams scored two TDs after that stop, so that one play didn't tilt the game by itself.

But Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley — filling in for an injured Saquon Barkley — had been running effectively on the drive, grinding away at the Rams. Hurts also is one of the better short-yardage running QBs in the game, although the Rams had stuffed a tush push late in the third quarter, which surely had to factor into Sirianni's thinking. It also didn't help that Hurts' timing on the third-and-goal play was thrown off by Cam Jurgens pulling too quickly, resulting in a no-gain.

Whether or not Sirianni made the right call, it backfired. Matthew Stafford looked down and out after his previous five possessions came up empty, but this was the spark he and his offense needed.

The Rams drove 98 yards on their ensuing drive to keep the game alive, and after the Eagles' 64-second three-and-out, the Rams went down and scored again for the improbable win .

The Eagles are in rough injury shape, and they've now lost two straight. Monday's loss in Chicago was a laugher, but they had Sunday's game in good shape before the late collapse.

3. Key INT, review help Packers hold off Bucs

In the final minute of the first half, the Bucs and Packers were tied at 7-all. Six game minutes later, the Bucs were down 10. Losing the middle portion of the game cost them dearly.

Rookie QB Jalon Daniels, filling in for an injured Baker Mayfield, threw a first-quarter interception, yet he was holding his own. Then Daniels threw his second pick of the first half, with Packers linebacker Edgerrin Cooper diving to make the grab and running it back 18 yards into Bucs territory.

That set up a Trey Smack 58-yard field goal and a little bump for the Packers before halftime. On their first possession of the second half, Jordan Love hit Tucker Kraft for a touchdown. Initially, it was called incomplete but later overturned after replay — and it was hardly obvious whether Kraft's foot clearly hit before he secured the catch.

It was an ugly game. Cooper left with an Achilles injury. Kaleb Johnson fumbled inside the 5-yard line. Love had a chance to make it a 10-point lead with four minutes left, but he threw an interception. The Packers were 2 for 10 on third downs.

The Bucs made their share of mistakes, too. But misplaying the middle section of the game, rookie quarterback or not, put them in an even tougher spot to pull off the upset .

The Raiders couldn't keep their unbeaten streak going, falling to the Chiefs , but they made Kansas City earn that victory in Las Vegas. Had a few more plays gone the Raiders' way, who knows?

Dareke Young's fumble on a kickoff, trailing 23-19 with 3:21 left in the game, was the obvious late momentum shift — and, yes, it hurt badly, even if the Raiders had a chance to tie or take the lead on their final drive.

But there was an earlier shift that cost the Raiders three points that head coach Klint Kubiak might now be regretting.

Three minutes into the second half, the Raiders' Matt Gay hit a 41-yard field goal to temporarily put the Raiders up 16-10. But the Chiefs were flagged for illegal formation on the kick, and Kubiak opted to take the points off the board — in spite of it not giving them an automatic first down.

Kirk Cousins' fourth-and-2 pass to Ashton Jeanty fell incomplete. The score remained 13-10, and the Raiders ended up losing by three points.

Kubiak might also regret predicting the Raiders would win during his halftime interview. Not too long later, his field-goal decision hurt his team.

5. Bell's nullified touchdown sunk Dolphins

There has been talk about the possibility of the Dolphins going winless this season, but with a few more breaks, they might have been able to take down the Vikings in Minnesota.

The biggest play that went against them was a tremendous touchdown that evaporated into thin air almost as fast as it happened.

Early in the second quarter, Malik Willis scrambled and — off-balance and falling out of bounds — threw what appeared to be a 68-yard TD to talented rookie wide receiver Chris Bell on a third-and-4 play. For the briefest of moments, Miami was leading 3-0, and the U.S. Bank Stadium crowd was stunned.

But Bell was flagged for illegal touching, having stepped out of bounds on his own prior to the catch, which wiped out what would have been his first career touchdown. The penalty came with a loss of downs, forcing a punt. The Vikings went down and kicked the second of their five field goals on the day in a 15-10 win.

Miami finished the first half with only 76 yards on 21 plays. The Dolphins' offense got going a bit with a 10-point third quarter, but that's all the group could muster. The Bell touchdown would have changed the game dramatically.

The Dolphins scored the only touchdown in the game — and they should have had two — but the Vikings held on for victory. That's how much separated the winless Dolphins and the unbeaten Vikings playing in their home stadium.

articles.title: “Every bone in his body cracked”: Chop Robinson escapes NFL fine after controversial Patrick Mahomes hit as the Kansas City Chiefs star reveals his condition
articles.summary: Chop Robinson came away from a controversial hit on Patrick Mahomes without an NFL fine.
articles.body: Chop Robinson came away from a controversial hit on Patrick Mahomes without an NFL fine. The Dolphins pass rusher drew a roughing-the-passer flag during Miami’s Week 3 game against the Kansas City Chiefs on Oct. 4, 2026. The call gave Kansas City a fresh set of downs, but Robinson avoided further punishment when the league released its Week 3 accountability report.The play came late in the third quarter with the Chiefs backed up at their own 5-yard line. Mahomes dropped back on third-and-9, and Robinson closed in from the edge just after the quarterback released a pass toward Rashee Rice. The pass fell incomplete, but Robinson drove Mahomes into the turf and drew the flag.Chop Robinson avoids NFL punishment after Patrick Mahomes collisionThe NFL released its Week 3 accountability report after the game, listing 30 plays that led to fines. Robinson did not appear among them. That kept the roughing call at an in-game penalty rather than turning it into an additional financial punishment.Robinson also accepted the call after the play, even though he admitted he did not know what else he could have done. Speaking after the game, the Dolphins pass rusher said, “I’m honestly not too sure, but either way, that’s what they called, so that’s what we got to play on. Next play.” He later added that he could have put his hands out earlier while falling.The penalty proved costly for Miami. The Chiefs would have faced a third-down stop deep in their own territory, but the penalty kept the drive alive. Kansas City then marched 80 yards on 13 plays, with Harrison Butker hitting a field goal that pushed the score to 17-10 in the fourth quarter. Patrick Mahomes walks away from Chop Robinson’s hit without missing timeThe collision looked concerning because Mahomes briefly grabbed his back after getting up. Still, the Chiefs quarterback stayed in the game and continued running the offense. Kansas City went on to beat Miami 24-10 and improved to 3-0.Chiefs head coach Andy Reid later joked about the force of the hit while discussing the quarterback’s ability to get back up. Speaking after the game, Reid said, “every bone in his body cracked,” before noting that Mahomes continued playing.Patrick Mahomes also brushed off the collision after the game. After the game, the QB said, “I’m doing great. It was like a natural chiropractor, so I felt better after the game, so I’m doing fine.”He finished with 246 passing yards, two touchdowns and one interception, and he did not miss a snap after Robinson’s hit.For Robinson, the NFL’s decision closes the issue without a fine. articles.body: Travis Kelce’s frustration with an NFL official cost him $24,309 in 2016. On Nov. 6, the Kansas City Chiefs tight end threw his towel toward an official during a 19-14 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars. The unusual move earned him a second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty and an ejection.The NFL announced Kelce’s fine on Nov. 11, 2016. Yet the Chiefs star did not let the hefty punishment end there. Instead, he turned the fine into a joke, asking fans on Twitter what he could buy with $24,309. His answer included 1,715 Nicolas Cage pillow cases.How a missed pass interference call started the incidentThe whole trouble began in the fourth quarter of the Nov. 6 game. Kelce believed Jaguars cornerback Prince Amukamara committed pass interference in the end zone, but officials did not throw a flag.Travis Kelce argued with two officials over the no-call. He received his first unsportsmanlike conduct penalty during the exchange. That still did not end his frustration.Kelce then pulled the towel from the waistband of his uniform and threw it toward an official. The gesture mocked the way officials throw penalty flags during games.Field Judge Mike Weatherford responded by throwing his cap toward Kelce. Another official then gave Kelce his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty, which resulted in his ejection.The Chiefs still won the game 19-14, but Kelce’s exit became one of the biggest talking points afterward.Kelce acknowledged that he had gone too far. Speaking after the Chiefs’ victory on November 6, he said, “I felt like an idiot. I can’t do that to my teammates. It was a terrible decision.”He also joked about the unusual exchange with the officials, saying, “I can’t throw my flag on the ref, but he can throw his all day long.” Travis Kelce turned the $24,309 fine into a jokeFive days after the game, the NFL handed Kelce a $24,309 fine for his conduct toward the official. The amount quickly became part of the story because Kelce found an unusual way to deal with it. After the league announced the fine, Travis Kelce went to Twitter and asked fans what he could purchase with $24,309. Among his calculations was a bizarre option: 1,715 Nicolas Cage pillow cases.The joke gave the incident a lighter ending, but Travis Kelce already had a history of NFL fines. In 2014, the league fined him $11,205 after he made an unsportsmanlike gesture near a referee who announced a penalty.The 2016 incident, however, had a different twist. articles.title: NFL reportedly 'looking into' official sharing words with Cardinals' Trey McBride after dispute over no-call
articles.summary: There were no microphones nearby, so what Seeman said is left strictly up to the interpretation of lip readers. But Seeman clearly wasn't telling McBride to...
articles.body:
NFL line judge Jeff Seeman had some choice words for Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride on Sunday and the league is reportedly looking into the incident.

CBS cameras caught those words, much to the delight of McBride who laughed and pointed it out as soon as he realized that a camera was pointed at the official during the Cardinals' game at the New York Giants.

There were no microphones nearby, so what Seeman said is left strictly up to the interpretation of lip readers. But Seeman clearly wasn't telling McBride to have a nice day.

The interaction caught the attention of NFL Players Association executive director JC Tretter, who called on the NFL to hold Seeman accountable while sharing video on social media of the incident.

"This kind of behavior from an official towards a player is unacceptable," Tretter wrote. "Players are consistently held accountable when the roles are reversed. We expect the NFL to hold officials to the same standard."

Shortly after Tretter's tweet, The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported that the NFL stated that it's "looking into the matter."

The interaction took place after game officials declined to call pass interference on a critical failed third-down pass from Jacoby Brissett to McBride. Giants cornerback Dru Phillips had coverage on the play and made contact with McBride before the ball arrived. McBride immediately protested the no-call to Seeman, who was standing next to the play. McBride's protests were to no avail and eventually drew the response seen above.

The Cardinals trailed 27-24 at the time of the incompletion and punted on the next play with 4:53 remaining in regulation. The Giants won the game 36-24.

McBride didn't address Seeman's comments with reporters postgame. The subject did not come up in the postgame pool report.

articles.title: Chiefs reportedly having discussions with Tyreek Hill about potential reunion after latest injuries
articles.summary: The stars are starting to align with a Chiefs-Tyreek Hill reunion after Sunday. The two sides have been in communication and with recent injuries the possibi...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs had a very important divisional game on Sunday as they went against the Las Vegas Raiders , who were also undefeated. In what was a very tight game, the Chiefs were able to escape with a road win.

Kansas City did suffer some major injuries to its WR room, with the first being Rashee Rice. Then, Tyquan Thornton suffered a dislocated ankle in the fourth quarter.

"Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton suffered a dislocated left ankle Sunday that was later put back into place by team doctors, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Thornton exited Allegiant Stadium on crutches after his team's 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. In the fourth quarter, he had to be carted off the field after he made a 55-yard catch that ended when he was tackled from behind by rookie free safety Treydan Stukes," ESPN's Nate Taylor wrote.

Despite the win, it came with a cost. The possibility of the Chiefs signing a WR is pretty high now. Taylor reported that the organization has been in contact with Tyreek Hill.

"Even before the injuries to Thornton and fellow receiver Rashee Rice on Sunday, the Chiefs had already shown interest in signing wide receiver Tyreek Hill, who is a free agent. Following Sunday's game, a team source said "we've remained in contact" with Hill and his agent Drew Rosenhaus," Taylor wrote.

This would be something, but the position is a necessity. At the beginning of September, Hill's agent Drew Rosenhaus gave a timeframe.

"Free-agent wide receiver Tyreek Hill and his representatives are "playing it on the safe side" as he prepares for a possible return to the NFL this season. His agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said Wednesday on The Pat McAfee Show that teams have shown interest in the eight-time Pro Bowler. However, doctors have advised Hill to delay a comeback until at least October," Bleacher Report's Joseph Zucker wrote.

It has been over a year since Hill's devastating injury to his leg, and it has been five years since his last game with Kansas City. This reunion would be one that the Chiefs need to make happen with their injuries.

Both sides will likely continue to discuss some things, but if Rice doesn't get a good report, it might be Hill's time to return to Kansas City. No one had this on their bingo card, and it very well could happen after the latest report.

articles.title: ‘This state belongs to Dallas’ – Fans erupt as Cowboys rally past Texans 34-30
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys fans erupted after their team came from behind to beat the Houston Texans 34-30 in a thrilling Texas showdown at NRG Stadium. The Cowboys trai...
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys fans erupted after their team came from behind to beat the Houston Texans 34-30 in a thrilling Texas showdown at NRG Stadium.

The Cowboys trailed 16-6 at half-time before turning the game around after the break. Dak Prescott eventually found CeeDee Lamb for the winning 12-yard touchdown with 40 seconds left.

Lamb was the star of the comeback, finishing with 17 catches for 189 yards and a touchdown. Javonte Williams also scored three rushing touchdowns as Dallas improved to 2-2.

Cowboys fans celebrate CeeDee Lamb after comeback win

Unsurprisingly, Lamb received plenty of praise from Cowboys supporters after his huge performance.

One fan simply posted: "WHAT A DAY FOR CEEDEE LAMB"

Another celebrated the comeback while already looking ahead to the reaction from Dallas supporters, writing: "down 10 at half and still won in Houston. Cowboys fans are gonna be unbearable this week"

Lamb's performance also prompted a bold declaration from another supporter: "CeeDee Lamb is the best wide receiver in the NFL"

The comeback meant plenty to Cowboys fans, with one writing: "I was fervently praying for you today!! Way to go Cowboys"

Another supporter highlighted the dramatic turnaround after half-time: "Cowboys really came alive in the 2nd half"

Houston had been unable to contain Lamb when it mattered most, prompting one fan to joke: "Texans couldn't 'silence the Lamb.'"

The win also sparked some classic Texas bragging rights, with one supporter declaring: "This state belongs to the Dallas Cowboys!!!"

Another took things even further, writing: "There's only one true king of Texas and the NFL… and that's my beloved Cowboys #DALvsHOU"

Dallas now sits at 2-2 after recovering from a difficult first half and will take plenty of confidence from the way Prescott and Lamb delivered when the game was on the line. For Houston, the loss leaves the Texans still searching for their first win after letting another late lead slip away.

articles.title: Kenneth Walker has transformed Kansas City Chiefs and unlocked Patrick Mahomes as Andy Reid's side stay perfect - NFL Sunday Review
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs extended their perfect start to the season while the Buffalo Bills defense endured more problems - Welcome to our weekly NFL Sunday Review; watch the Jacksonville Jaguars against the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium live on Sky Sports next Sunday
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs are a perfect 4-0, Patrick Mahomes is once again attacking defences downfield, and Kenneth Walker III has transformed the identity of Andy Reid's offense. The NFL thought it had finally slayed the monster, only for it to grow another head.

For now, this is Walker's team, Walker's offense and Walker's show. Mahomes certainly won't mind, with the NFL's best quarterback shining once again while benefiting from his running back's remarkable early-season form.

Walker was decisive once again on Sunday, rushing for 177 yards and two touchdowns to lift Kansas City to a thrilling 30-27 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders. The performance also saw him retain his place as the NFL's leading rusher, continuing a remarkable start to his first season with the Chiefs following his move in free agency.

"He's a game-changer. He did that for us today," said Mahomes.

Walker's 537 rushing yards are now the most by any running back through the first four games of a season over the last 15 years, surpassing DeMarco Murray's 534-yard mark from 2014, according to Pro Football Focus .

It has been a long time since the Chiefs have had such a blue-chip weapon alongside Mahomes. Since the departure of Tyreek Hill, Kansas City's superstar quarterback has often had to carry an offense that lacked a true game-changing threat. Walker has already shown he can be the missing piece.

Walker has blown the door to play-action and field-stretching success off its hinges, giving the Chiefs a new dimension out of the backfield and breathing life into an offense that, incredibly, had become borderline unwatchable at times under Mahomes in recent years.

Patient yet electric, Walker possesses tremendous vision and the ability to make would-be tacklers miss better than almost any back in football. He is precisely the outlet Mahomes and Reid have been craving.

One of the highlights came during a mazy second-quarter run. Walker exploded to his left, shrugged off one tackle attempt, juked inside two more defenders and then powered through another cluster of bodies to pick up a crucial first down.

Later, he found a perfectly placed crease and burst through it, racing 76 yards for the longest run by any player in the NFL this season. Walker reached a top speed of 21.21mph, according to Next Gen Stats, with the explosive play setting up Tyquan Thornton's eight-yard touchdown catch to put Kansas City 17-13 ahead early in the fourth quarter.

And how fitting that Walker should be the one to ice the game. The February Super Bowl MVP first powered in from two yards out to give the Chiefs a 23-19 advantage, before capitalising on a Raiders fumble with a spectacular 20-yard dive for the pylon.

Two touchdowns in the space of just 19 seconds.

Already, Walker is putting together an Offensive Player of the Year-calibre campaign as the heartbeat of a revitalised Chiefs offense. His impact extends beyond his own touches, with the threat of his presence opening up space and opportunity for Mahomes to rediscover his magic.

With Sunday's victory, the Chiefs are now the AFC's last unbeaten team following Buffalo's defeat to New England. They are on course to return to the playoffs after missing out for the first time since 2014 last season.

Reid and Mahomes are back with a vengeance, and they may have found the perfect mercenary in Walker to help exorcise the demons of the past.

The Buffalo Bills' defense remains a problem . Jim Leonhard's unit entered the season under the microscope, tasked with matching the brilliance of quarterback Josh Allen and providing the production needed on the other side of the ball to finally push Buffalo over the Super Bowl hump. Aside from Greg Rousseau's lightning-fast start, however, the defense has struggled to make a meaningful impact.

The Bills surrendered 405 total yards and 26 first downs in Sunday's 29-26 defeat to the New England Patriots, suffering their first loss of the season against a supposedly struggling Drake Maye and looking increasingly vulnerable in the process. Buffalo remains a team that is difficult to trust.

The Eagles' offensive problems are still very real . Kevin Patullo took plenty of criticism last season for his role in an offense that struggled behind Jalen Hurts, eventually losing his job as offensive coordinator in the offseason and being replaced by Sean Mannion.

Yet the problems have not disappeared. The Eagles managed just seven points in last week's defeat to the Case Keenum-led Chicago Bears and could muster only 172 total yards in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams - their fewest in a game since Week 14 of the 2014 season.

Hurts threw for just 93 yards, including only 10 after half-time. There were mitigating factors, with Philadelphia missing both DeVonta Smith and Dalton Schultz, while Saquon Barkley was sidelined for more than half the game. Even so, it has been an undeniably difficult fortnight for Nick Sirianni's team.

The Raiders may have the best tight end duo in football. The Chiefs were understandably committed to containing Brock Bowers on Sunday, but doing so created opportunities for Michael Mayer to punish them within Klint Kubiak's multiple tight end sets.

Mayer made eight catches for 82 yards in one of the best performances of his NFL career, while he and Bowers combined for 168 receiving yards. Mayer's presence gave Kubiak the freedom to move his star tight end around the formation and create mismatches.

In truth, Bowers is often deployed more like a big-bodied receiver than a traditional tight end, such is the absurdity of his physical gifts. On several occasions Sunday, he was used simply as a body-clearing decoy to create space underneath - a role typically reserved for a player who commands an extraordinary level of defensive attention.

Behind Mayer and Bowers, the Raiders and Kirk Cousins went toe-to-toe with the Chiefs, showcasing an offense capable of competing with - and hurting - the league's best.

Todd Bowles' tenure as Tampa Bay Buccaneers head coach is over.

If it isn't already, it feels increasingly inevitable.

Tampa Bay fell to 0-4 for the first time since 2013 on Sunday after suffering a 17-14 defeat to the Green Bay Packers. With Baker Mayfield sidelined by a thumb injury, the situation could get even worse.

Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels was handed the reins and completed 19 of 27 passes for 148 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. But with Mayfield unavailable and the losses piling up, the Buccaneers' season is already threatening to unravel.

Their biggest saving grace? They play in the NFC South - a division that, at this stage, nobody seems particularly interested in winning.

Drake Maye: How about that for a response? Drake Maye was written off after the first three weeks of the season following a difficult start in the aftermath of New England's Super Bowl nightmare in February. But he responded emphatically this weekend, leading the Patriots to a statement victory over the Bills. Maye finished 22 of 37 for 269 yards, three touchdowns and one interception, while adding 54 rushing yards. Nerves calmed... for now.

Zay Flowers: Rightly or wrongly, the jury remains out on whether Zay Flowers can be a legitimate needle-mover in Baltimore's Super Bowl pursuit. When he is firing, however, he is a genuine difference-maker for Lamar Jackson and the Ravens offense. Electric as a downfield playmaker and outstanding at creating separation, Flowers added 118 yards and a touchdown in his side's 24-18 victory over the Tennessee Titans. Keeping Flowers healthy for an entire season will be crucial to Declan Doyle's chances of success.

DeMeco Ryans: It once seemed unfathomable that DeMeco Ryans would find himself under any kind of pressure in his role as Houston Texans head coach, but an 0-4 start will do that. Nico Collins provided a bright spot with 117 yards and two touchdowns on his return from injury, but even Houston's star-studded defense could not hold up its end of the bargain in a 34-30 defeat to the Cowboys.

The Eagles and London: The Eagles were dealt a potentially significant blow in their defeat to the Rams after losing star running back Saquon Barkley to a reported hamstring injury. Barkley missed more than three quarters of the game, adding to the existing absence of DeVonta Smith with Philadelphia now just one week away from facing the Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham.

Player of the Weekend - Byron Young, EDGE, Los Angeles Rams

No Myles Garrett? No Aaron Donald? No Jared Verse? No problem.

The strength of Chris Shula's Los Angeles Rams defense last season was the sheer breadth and depth of its pass-rushing options, led by Verse before his offseason trade to the Cleveland Browns. On Sunday, it was Byron Young's turn to underline his importance, producing 2.5 sacks, six tackles, two tackles for loss, three quarterback hits and a forced fumble in the victory over the Philadelphia Eagles.

The Cowboys emerged victorious in the Battle of Texas, overturning a 16-6 half-time deficit to defeat the Houston Texans 34-30 in a thriller that showcased every aspect of their offensive firepower.

CeeDee Lamb was the star, hauling in 17 catches for 189 yards and a touchdown, including 140 yards after the break. Dak Prescott completed 32 of 45 passes for 335 yards and a touchdown, while Javonte Williams added three rushing touchdowns against Houston's elite defense.

articles.title: NFL: Kansas City Chiefs, San Francisco 49ers & Minnesota Vikings stay unbeaten - week four round-up
articles.summary: Five teams went into week four of the NFL season with a 100% record, but only three teams remain unbeaten after Sunday's action.
articles.body:
Only three teams remain unbeaten in the NFL after two more 100% starts were halted during week four of the season.

Sunday's slate got under way with the Indianapolis Colts beating the Washington Commanders in the first of this season's three London games.

The New England Patriots and Los Angeles Rams then avoided dropping to a 1-3 record by pulling off some big wins on the road.

The Kansas City Chiefs and Las Vegas Raiders were among the five teams who made a 3-0 start to the season and one team's '0' had to go as the divisional rivals met, while the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings marched on.

Here are five things you missed from Sunday's action.

Kansas City have dominated their rivalry with the Raiders in recent years, but Las Vegas are vastly improved after winning only three games last season and pushed the Chiefs all the way.

The Raiders led 13-10 heading into the final quarter in Vegas, which featured three lead changes before Kansas City held on for a 30-27 win.

The turning point came as new running back Kenneth Walker maintained his stunning start by scoring two touchdowns in 19 seconds, with the Chiefs regaining possession immediately by forcing a fumble on the kick-off return.

The Raiders gave themselves hope with a Brock Bowers score and stayed alive until the final play, when Kirk Cousins was tackled as he threw and his wayward pass was intercepted.

Walker finished with 177 yards from 22 carries, while team-mate Tyquan Thornton also had two touchdowns and 111 receiving yards.

After missing last season's play-offs, the Chiefs look capable of getting back into Super Bowl contention. They next face the Los Angeles Chargers, who are 0-4 after losing 30-23 to defending champions the Seattle Seahawks.

The other two teams who improved to 4-0 were the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings.

The 49ers hosted the Denver Broncos, who overcame Super Bowl favourites the Rams last week, and they were tied 3-3 until late in the third quarter.

Christian McCaffrey's touchdown in the fourth quarter gave the 49ers some breathing space and, although Jaylen Waddle replied, George Kittle scored on a huge catch-and-run down the middle to seal a 24-14 win.

While Cousins and Brock Purdy lead the league with 11 touchdown passes, Purdy has been intercepted only once and has not been sacked in the 49ers' first four games.

The Vikings are the biggest surprise to be 4-0, having ground out another win, this time 15-10 over the Miami Dolphins, with Will Reichard kicking five field goals.

Some said Drake Maye's confidence was shot after he was benched during the New England Patriots' blowout loss at the Jacksonville Jaguars last week.

After throwing eight interceptions in the 2025 regular season, the 24-year-old quarterback had six in the Patriots' first three games and only one touchdown pass.

Next up was a daunting trip to the unbeaten Buffalo Bills - led by the 2024 Most Valuable Player Josh Allen - but Maye showed why he narrowly missed out on the MVP award last season, when he led the Patriots to an unexpected Super Bowl run.

After Allen restored Buffalo's lead with a 34-yard touchdown pass to Keon Coleman with four minutes left, Efton Chism made a superb one-handed catch in the endzone to put the Patriots back in front.

They then intercepted a hopeful Allen throw to clinch a 29-26 win, with Maye passing for three touchdowns and 269 yards.

The Bills joined the Rams as Super Bowl favourites last week and they go head to head in LA next week.

Another Eagles injury before London trip

After losing a thriller at Denver last Monday, the LA Rams were 1-2 and faced another stern test on the road this week at the Philadelphia Eagles.

The hosts led 20-10 at half-time after two Darius Cooper touchdowns, but the Rams fought back, with Kyren Williams rushing for two touchdowns in the final four minutes to claim a 24-20 victory.

The fit-again Puka Nacua finished with 125 receiving yards and a touchdown for the Rams, while the Eagles' injury concerns mounted.

Wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring) was ruled out before the game, joining tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) on the sidelines, and Philadelphia lost star running back Saquon Barkley to an early hamstring injury.

That is a big blow for the Eagles and UK fans as they visit Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Sunday to face the Jacksonville Jaguars, who beat the Cincinnati Bengals 22-17 to make it back-to-back wins.

The Baltimore Ravens also have fitness concerns over a key man, with two-time MVP Lamar Jackson (ankle) unable to play during the second half of their 24-18 home win against the Tennessee Titans.

When are the 2026 NFL London games taking place?

There have been at least 48 points in every Dallas Cowboys game this season, and they played their part in another high-scoring affair at state rivals Houston.

The Texans led 23-13 after Nico Collins' second score in the third quarter and then 30-27 with two minutes remaining.

But Dak Prescott led the Cowboys to a game-winning drive of 11 plays and 74 yards, throwing a touchdown pass to star receiver CeeDee Lamb to claim a 34-30 win.

Lamb had a career-high 17 receptions for 189 yards, while team-mate Javonte Williams rushed for three touchdowns as Dallas improved to 2-2.

Sunday's highest scorers were the New York Giants after Jameis Winston, filling in for injured quarterback Jaxson Dart, threw three touchdowns and two interceptions in a 36-24 win at home to the Arizona Cardinals.

articles.title: NFL Week 4: Redeemed QBs, the AFC’s best (so far) and the record streak that finally died
articles.summary: Week 4 of the NFL season featured dramatic fourth-quarter comebacks, quarterbacks who redeemed themselves, quarterbacks who continued to struggle and three teams left standing with undefeated records.
articles.body: Week 4 of the NFL season featured dramatic fourth-quarter comebacks, quarterbacks who redeemed themselves, quarterbacks who continued to struggle and three teams left standing with undefeated records. Here’s all the action you need to know about from Sunday. Redemption for Drake Maye The first three weeks of the season were forgettable for New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye. The beleaguered signal-caller entered Sunday with only one touchdown, six interceptions and seven total turnovers through three games. Facing the undefeated Buffalo Bills on the road, Maye had his best game of the season, throwing for a season-best 269 yards and three touchdowns to lead the Patriots to a 26-21 victory. Maye also led New England in rushing with 54 yards in a well-rounded performance. He outplayed his counterpart, Josh Allen, who finished with only 253 passing yards and threw a pick on a potential game-winning drive. Maye led two go-ahead drives in the second half, including an eight-play, 73-yard jaunt in the fourth quarter that ended with the play of the game. New England improved to 2-2, while the Bills fell to 3-1. Another stinker for Justin Herbert Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert was also looking for a bounceback performance Sunday. He didn’t find one. Herbert had three turnovers as the Chargers lost 30-23 to the Seattle Seahawks, dropping Los Angeles to 0-4. Herbert threw two interceptions — his second multi-pick game in four weeks — and on a potential game-winning drive, he fumbled when he fell victim to blindside pressure. The loss continued a rough season for Herbert. His passer rating of 73.4 entering Sunday will drop after he posted a 62.4 rating in Seattle, and he’s on pace for a career low in that category. Herbert is also averaging career-worst marks in completion percentage and yards per game. The hiring of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel has yet to unlock Herbert, who is lauded by league personnel for his physical tools. To make matters worse for the Chargers, their schedule doesn’t let up anytime soon. Over the next five weeks, Los Angeles will play the Denver Broncos, the Kansas City Chiefs, the Los Angeles Rams, the Houston Texans and the Baltimore Ravens. Only one of those teams (the Texans) has a losing record. The rest are a combined 11-5. Don’t sleep on the Jacksonville Jaguars Are the Jaguars sneakily the best team in the AFC? Jacksonville improved to 3-1 with a 22-17 win over the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 4. The Jags’ three wins have all come against solid quarterbacks: Joe Burrow, Maye and (a surprisingly competent) Deshaun Watson. Since Week 11 of last season, Jacksonville is 11-1 in the regular season. Including the playoffs, the Jags’ only two losses in that time have come by a combined 10 points. Quarterbacks beware: Jacksonville’s defense has six interceptions through four games. The Cowboys didn’t waste a great game from Dak Prescott The Dallas Cowboys improved to 2-2 by winning the battle of Texas, taking down the Houston Texans 34-30 in a back-and-forth game. Quarterback Dak Prescott continued his stellar play through the early part of the season. He has now thrown for eight touchdowns and only one interception through four weeks. He’s averaging 266.3 passing yards per game, and Dallas has scored at least 31 points in each of its last three games. Prescott leaned heavily on receiver CeeDee Lamb on Sunday, connecting with him 17 times for 189 yards. The Cowboys’ defense also did just enough to secure the victory, despite giving up at least 28 points for the third time in four weeks. The Texans fell to 0-4, unable to capitalize on C.J. Stroud’s 347 passing yards and two scores. Case Keenum improves to 2-0 as the Bears’ starter Keenum played only one snap for the Chicago Bears on Sunday: the opening one. He got to play what head coach Ben Johnson cheekily described as the “ceremonial first pitch.” He was then immediately replaced by Tyson Bagent, who partnered with a steady rushing attack to lead Chicago to a 23-13 win over the New York Jets. The Bears are now 2-0 without starter Caleb Williams. One streak ends ... It took 21 games, but a New York Jets streak at last ended Sunday. When Minkah Fitzpatrick stepped in front of a pass by Chicago’s Tyson Bagent, it was the first interception by a Jets player in an NFL-record 20 games. The Jets hadn’t gotten a pick since Jan. 5, 2025. That also made it the first interception since Aaron Glenn, a former NFL defensive back, took over as head coach. “We got an interception; great,” Glenn said. “We lost the game.” ... and another streak continues The Arizona Cardinals had a rare opportunity Sunday not only to win, but to beat a good team. Instead, after the New York Giants returned an interception in the final seconds to seal a 36-24 victory, one of the league’s most ignominious streaks grew. Arizona has lost 17 consecutive games against teams that entered with winning records, the league’s longest active losing streak, according to NBC Sports research. Under first-year coach Mike LaFleur, the Cardinals have been competitive in three of their four games and shown the kind of life that wasn’t necessarily expected entering a season when they were picked as a likely contender to earn the No. 1 overall pick. If the team does turn a corner under LaFleur, beating a winning team will be a cathartic milestone. The 49ers, Vikings and Chiefs remain undefeated Three undefeated teams are left in the NFL. The Kansas City Chiefs improved to 4-0 by holding off a frisky Las Vegas Raiders team, which entered their divisional matchup undefeated themselves. The San Francisco 49ers beat the Broncos at home, while the Minnesota Vikings kicked five field goals in a 15-10 win over the Miami Dolphins. Panthers perform on rare primetime stage During Carolina’s first appearance on “Sunday Night Football” since 2016, Panthers quarterback Bryce Young continued his career rebound in a 32-26 win over Detroit. Young, the former No. 1 overall pick, completed his first 11 passes and finished with 29 completions in 41 attempts for 329 yards and two touchdowns to Tetairola McMillan. Operating often from the slot, McMillan continued a huge day for receivers by catching 14 passes, including those two touchdowns, for 192 yards. Young was 2-14 as a rookie in 2023 and he was benched the next season, but he helped Carolina make the playoffs last season. Through four games this fall, his 1,268 passing yards leads the NFL. The Panthers had lost five of their last six games before they held on late with a defensive stand.
