articles.title: NFL Week 4 Sunday takeaways: Cowboys get season-defining win over Texans, 49ers are league's best team
articles.summary: The Cowboys scored 28 second-half points to stun the Texans, who fell to 0-4 after blowing a double-digit lead in a potential season-defining clash.
articles.body: We've reached October, which means "it's still early" is starting to do a lot of heavy lifting for some NFL fan bases. There's plenty of football left, obviously, but at some point your team has to actually win a game instead of telling everyone it's going to be fine (it's not going to be fine, Chargers fans). Meanwhile, I'm back with another round of opinions that could look brilliant or incredibly stupid by next Sunday (yeah, about that Drake Maye comment last Sunday ...). That's part of the fun. At least, that's what I tell myself. Here's my biggest takeaway from each game on the Week 4 Sunday slate. Colts 30, Commanders 13 Takeaway: That Jonathan Taylor guy is pretty good. It's hard to glean too much from a game where the Commanders were forced to go to their third-string quarterback after Marcus Mariota suffered a knee injury in the first quarter. Instead, I'm going to sing the praises of Jonathan Taylor, who has six rushing touchdowns in four games and plays a very old-school game. That's cool because a few years ago, we thought old-school running backs were done in the NFL. Taylor and Derrick Henry, in particular, aren't going to let that happen any time soon. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Giants 36, Cardinals 24 Takeaway: How can any NFL fan not love Jameis Winston eating a W? Without Jaxson Dart, the Giants aren't a threat to make a deep run in the postseason. They probably won't even make the postseason. But right now, who cares? The Giants are 3-1 and currently in first place in the NFC East. Plus, they've got the Commanders in Week 5, and Washington's uncertain QB situation could make that task quite a bit easier. It might not last, but Giants fans should enjoy the early success. Patriots 29, Bills 26 Takeaway: As soon as you think you know something, the NFL reminds you that you don't. Of course, the 1–2 Patriots, who looked awful in Week 3, went into Buffalo and beat the previously unbeaten Bills as seven-point underdogs. Because of course. This is the type of game that makes the NFL great. Just when you think you have a handle on which teams are good and which teams are bad, the NFL says, "You don't know what you think you know." Bears 23, Jets 12 Takeaway: Ben Johnson is a damn genius. Look, I'm not going to overreact to the Bears beating the Jets. But regardless of opponent, Chicago head coach Ben Johnson just went 2-0 with Case Keenum starting in Week 3 and Tyson Bagent starting in Week 4. For the record, entering this stretch, neither Keenum nor Bagent had even started an NFL regular-season game since 2023. The defense deserves a lot of credit (and Johnson deserves credit for hiring Dennis Allen as his defensive coordinator), but scoring 50 points with those two QBs shows that Johnson is one of the league’s sharpest offensive minds. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Cowboys 34, Texans 30 Takeaway: If it's possible for an October game to be a season-defining game, this was it ... for both teams. This is the type of win that the Cowboys can use to build momentum, especially with two winnable games coming up against the Buccaneers and Packers. Scoring 28 second-half points against one of the league's best defenses is exactly the type of thing that can instill confidence in an offense for the rest of the season. On the other side, I don't know how the Texans recover from this. Not only did they fall to 0-4, but they blew a double-digit second-half lead and allowed the Cowboys to take the lead with an 11-play, 74-yard drive in just 1:43 right after Houston had retaken the lead. Only one team in NFL history has made the playoffs after starting 0-4: the 1992 San Diego Chargers. So, not only do they have to reverse a 34-year-old trend, but they have to do it coming off one of Houston's most heartbreaking losses in recent memory. Rams 24, Eagles 20 Takeaway: Speaking of heartbreaking losses, my goodness, Philadelphia. The good news for the Eagles is that, unlike the Texans, their heartbreaking blown double-digit second-half lead dropped them to 2-2 instead of 0-4. The bad news is that it probably doesn't make them feel any better. I've said for three weeks that the Eagles are a deeply flawed team, but their record said otherwise. Now, their 2-2 record feels more appropriate. Packers 17, Buccaneers 14 Takeaway: Both of these teams are bad. This felt like a must-win for the Packers against a bad Bucs team starting a backup quarterback. And, credit to them, they got it done. But they didn't make it easy on themselves, didn't look good doing it, and nearly blew it late. Todd Bowles is probably on his way out in Tampa, but Matt LaFleur's seat might start to heat up if Green Bay doesn't start playing better, particularly on offense, over the next month. Ravens 24, Titans 18 Takeaway: I got nothing. It doesn't appear that Lamar Jackson's ankle injury is too serious, and it's hard to fault the Ravens for being careful with their star quarterback in a game they were never in danger of losing. Aside from that, I got nothing. The Ravens are pretty good, the Titans are pretty bad, and Sunday's game pretty much showed exactly that. Credit to Tennessee for fighting until the final whistle, though. Jaguars 22, Bengals 17 Takeaway: Neither team should be too excited about this game. Yes, the Jaguars are obviously much happier after going into Cincinnati and upsetting the Bengals. But they committed 13 penalties for 125 yards and nearly allowed Cincinnati to pull off a miraculous comeback with some puzzling late-game decisions. The Bengals lost Ja'Marr Chase to a concussion early in the second quarter, and Tee Higgins left the game late after suffering an adductor injury. Oh, and they committed 11 penalties of their own for 108 yards. It was an ugly, ugly game, but the focus in Cincinnati turns to the health of their two star receivers. Vikings 15, Dolphins 10 Takeaway: Is Minnesota the most fraudulent 4-0 team ever? Probably not, but I don't have time to go through every 4-0 team in NFL history. That being said, this team is not nearly as good as its record. They beat the Packers (who aren't good), the Bears (who are good, but that was a weird game played in a massive rainstorm), the Bucs (who aren't good) and the Dolphins (who, guess what? Aren't good). At the end of the day, it doesn't really matter, I guess. There are plenty of teams that would rather be a fraudulent 4-0 than have their current record. Chiefs 30, Raiders 27 Takeaway: The Raiders might actually be decent. Yes, the Chiefs won to move to 4-0. It's fair to say that Kansas City is officially "back." But everyone is going to say that, so let's take some time to talk about the Raiders. Las Vegas had a lead in every quarter, including the fourth. But two plays changed everything: a 55-yard pass to Tyquan Thornton on third-and-5 with 3:35 left (to set up a go-ahead touchdown on the next play) and a Raiders fumble on the ensuing kick return. Those moments shouldn't distract from the fact that Las Vegas looked every bit as good as the Chiefs for most of the game, and at certain points, better. This isn't the 2025 Raiders anymore. Seahawks 30, Chargers 23 Takeaway: Things are going to get worse before they get better. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Seattle bounced back from a surprising Week 3 upset loss against Washington, but the real test comes next week in a measuring-stick showdown against San Francisco. For the Chargers, there's just not much light at the end of the tunnel. They fell to 0-4, the season is basically over, and if that weren't bad enough, here's the upcoming schedule: Broncos, Chiefs, Rams, Texans, Ravens. For a team with Super Bowl aspirations coming into the season, Los Angeles could be staring down the barrel of an 0-9 start if they don't figure something out in a hurry. 49ers 24, Broncos 14 Takeaway: The San Francisco 49ers are the best team in the NFL. I'm not just saying that because they beat the overrated Broncos (and their insanely overrated head coach). Sure, the win helps bolster the case. But San Francisco is now 4-0 with three wins by double digits and a fourth that would have been a nine-point win if not for a virtually meaningless late field goal last week. Yes, they have played the Dolphins and Cardinals. But they also blasted the Super Bowl-favorite Rams and now boast a ridiculous +58 point differential. The Rams got all the preseason hype, but it was their NFC West rivals that everyone should have been worried about. Panthers 32, Lions 26 Takeaway: Sometimes a good benching is all you need. It's crazy to think that the Bryce Young, who completed 29 of 41 passes for 329 yards, two touchdowns and no turnovers against the Lions on Sunday Night Football, is the same quarterback we saw two years ago. Entering Week 3 of the 2024 NFL season, it seemed like Carolina Panthers fans and the franchise were ready to give up on Young, the No. 1 pick in the 2023 NFL Draft. He had earned the dreaded "bust" label after posting a 2-16 record as a starter with more interceptions (13) than passing touchdowns (11). The team benched him for that Week 3 game in 2024 and he didn't return to the starting lineup until Week 8. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Since then, Young's been a different player. He led the team to an NFC South title in 2025 and has gone 14-16 in regular-season starts since his return, throwing 47 passing touchdowns against 19 interceptions. This year, Carolina has one of the most explosive offenses in the league. If Young can go from benched in 2024 to back-to-back division titles, it'd be one of the best career turnarounds in NFL history.

articles.title: NFL's dumbest moment of Week 4 goes to a referee now on the Mount Rushmore of angrily jumping to conclusions
articles.summary: NFL referee Adrian Hill is under league review after getting knocked down during the Minnesota Vikings game and appearing to react angrily.
articles.body: Sometimes it's a defender that blows it, and sometimes it's a player on offense. There are even times when an NFL coach will say or do something really dumb that makes news. But when a referee does something ridiculous, well, we kind of have to pay extra attention. Meet Adrian Hill. First we noticed him on Sunday, he was on the ground after getting run over by players during the Minnesota Vikings game against the Miami Dolphins. And he was evidently really peeved about it. NFL'S MOST DEBATED WEEK 3 CALL HAS PEOPLE WONDERING HOW TO DEFY GRAVITY WHEN HITTING PATRICK MAHOMES Hill and the play that drew attention to him are being reviewed by the NFL on Monday, a league official confirmed to OutKick. The reason for the review is that Hill seemed to either: Hill did all this without realizing one key detail: Wilson was actually pushed into the official from behind by a Miami Dolphins player. And Wilson merely tried to help Hill get up afterward, as the ref was aggressively pointing at him to get away. Hill, you should know, is no rookie official. He's been in the NFL since 2010 and has been a referee since 2019. But despite that experience, he seemed to lose his composure after getting knocked down. NFL AND REFEREES UNION CLOSE IN ON AVOIDING POTENTIAL REPLACEMENT OFFICIALS NIGHTMARE The play happened in a regionally telecast game. But it drew national attention because of the NFL's review and the terrible optics of the moment online. And since it was online, fans decided to have an opinion about it. This is the part where you realize that fans having opinions does not include NFL referee fans. Because there are no known such beings on the planet. We're talking fans of the Vikings, of Wilson, even of poise amid adversity. Hill and his officiating colleagues have no fans. So, the reactions online were predictable. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! One NFL reporter posted that Hill "flipped out" over an "unintentional collision." "Officials have a hard job but their arrogance and opinions of themselves just make them so unlikable," former New York Jets offensive coordinator Scott Turner added. "Very sad," NFL agent Peter Shaffer posted. "Would never see an NHL referee act like this. Pathetic." NFL REVIEWING INCIDENT AFTER LINE JUDGE JEFF SEEMAN APPEARED TO HURL PROFANITY AT CARDINALS TREY MCBRIDE Sunday was a bad day for NFL officials and the attention they drew. In New York, the son of the league's former supervisor of officials was captured on television apparently cursing at Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride. The league is looking into that one also but there seems to be a theme in these two incidents. articles.title: Tyquan Thornton Makes Encouraging Post After Gruesome Ankle Injury in Chiefs' Win vs. Raiders
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton remained in high spirits after suffering an ankle injury in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton remained in high spirits after suffering an ankle injury in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Las Vegas Raiders.

Thornton posted on social media he'll "be back stronger & better."

New NFL contenders starting to emerge after Week 4

NFL investigating 2 referees for separate viral exchanges

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported the fifth-year pass-catcher dislocated his ankle. While a recovery timeline isn't yet known, an injury this serious is likely to rule him out for most or all of the remaining season.

Thornton was in the midst of a career day. Prior to exiting, he had five receptions for 111 yards and two touchdowns.

"His attitude is unbelievable," coach Andy Reid said of Thornton, per ESPN's Nate Taylor . "He's great for the team and kind of a leader of that [receivers] group. Thornton signed a two-year, $11 million contract with Kansas City, so he'll have the opportunity to rebuild his on-field value in 2027 before he hits free agency again.

The Kansas City Chiefs are "very interested" in a reunion with free-agent wide receiver Tyreek Hill, according to The Athletic's Michael Silver .

articles.title: The novelty might be wearing off for the NFL in London. A dire game between the Colts and Commanders didn’t help
articles.summary: NFL games in London used to be a hot ticket, but cut-rate prices and a poor product on the field is raising the question whether the novelty is wearing off.
articles.body: As Indianapolis Colts QB Daniel Jones and Washington Commanders signal-caller Athan Kaliakmanis traded overthrows, interceptions and fumbles, one question was surely going through everyone’s heads: Can you have too much of a good thing? William Shakespeare was certainly not thinking about NFL international games when writing his 1623 comedy As You Like It, but it’s not difficult to see why the playwright’s famous phrase could apply to this exact situation – albeit just a few hundred years too early. Not-so-hot property International NFL tickets were once one of the most coveted to get a hold of when it came to sports across the globe. Stories of tens of thousands of fans queuing up – virtually – to get their hands on the goods had become the norm, ending with more people being left bitterly disappointed than attending the games. However, when it was announced that the Commanders and the Colts were making the trip across the pond, the usual eagerness was a lot harder to come across. Tickets were still available the night before the big day, with fans not exactly rushing to fill up the vacant seats at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. And this was after the prices had already been massively reduced. Fans who had shown interest in the international games received emails a few weeks before the game detailing new low-priced tickets with the get-in price now advertised at just £79.13 (about $105), a far cry from what they had originally been listed for – and it didn’t stop there. For supporters who had left it particularly last-minute, tickets were available at an incredible price of just £9.95 (about $13.17). While some cashed in on the bargain prices, others understandably were left disappointed after already purchasing tickets at their original prices. In the buildup to the game, fans flocked to social media to share stories of their disappointment, some exasperated about paying more than double what someone sitting next to them may have paid. CNN Sports has reached out to Ticketmaster and the NFL for comment on fan frustrations. Unsurprisingly, with a cost-of-living crisis sweeping through the United Kingdom, asking fans to spend a lot of money to see two middling teams was always going to be a tough sell. It’s no surprise then that the stadium was largely full exclusively of Commanders and Colts fans, a sight that has rarely been seen before across international games in London. Train platforms and pubs on game days are usually packed with a visual cacophony of NFL jerseys, past and present, from franchises all across the league. But this time it was different. Washington’s burgundy and gold dominated the surrounding streets and the stands at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium with a smattering of Indianapolis blue playing second fiddle. This was the 43rd NFL game that London has hosted, and one could be forgiven for thinking that the novelty is now perhaps starting to wear off on everyday NFL fans in the UK. In fact, the loudest cheer of the first half came when the big screen asked fans who had traveled from the US to make some noise – seemingly an insight into how packed the stadium was with diehard fans who had made the long trip across the pond to see their team play. An error-strewn Sunday While there had already been problems off the field in the buildup, the on-field events did little to inspire the neutral. On the first drive and just the second snap of the contest, Colts QB Jones immediately treated fans in London to an incredible fumble. Jones tripped over his own left tackle Bernhard Raimann before dropping the ball on his way to the ground in a move that seemed to play out in slow motion. Washington, however, failed to capitalize on the advantageous field position it was gifted and had to settle for an early field goal instead. It was a sign of things to come. Commanders fans had already accepted they wouldn’t be seeing their starting quarterback and star player Jayden Daniels, but things quickly went from bad to worse as they lost backup Marcus Mariota to an early knee injury. Third-string quarterback Kaliakmanis was then thrown into the game in the most unusual of surroundings and, alongside his Colts counterpart, struggled to get any real offense going. As the clock ticked down towards the end of the opening quarter, a graphic popped up on the big screens to let everyone know that Indianapolis and Jones had thrown for -2 passing yards. Somehow, it felt like it was even less. Things didn’t get much better as the half went on, but the ever-reliable Jonathan Taylor rushed the Colts down the field before going on to score the opening touchdown of the game. There were, however, a few bright sparks in the second half of action that perked fans up. Taylor rushed for another touchdown as he continued with his impressive season to extend the Colts’ lead. Kaliakmanis started launching deep throws down the field and picked out Treylon Burks for the first touchdown pass of his career before Jones stormed home for the Colts’ third rushing touchdown of the encounter to reinforce the team’s advantage. With a couple of field goals somewhere in between from Indy’s Spencer Shrader, the Colts were victorious in the end, picking up a 30-13 win. It was far from a classic outing and one that ended up ultimately being worthy of the cheap, last-minute get-in prices. But despite the loss and lack of star power on the field, it would be fair to say that Washington fans did their best to make the game feel special. The noise at times was deafening from the Commanders faithful and deserving of better quality on the field. Is there a problem or is this a blip? When teams head overseas, it should feel special. Some fans wait a lifetime to see their favorite team in the flesh, with stars from across the league just a stone’s throw away and not on a TV in random times of the day, sometimes very late at night. But a game like this didn’t make it feel like the greatest show in town, which it should do, particularly with a more veteran NFL-going crowd like the British fans. The NFL seems intent on bringing more and more games to its overseas audience, but in doing so, is there a danger of oversaturating the market? CNN Sports has reached out to the NFL for comment on its overseas strategy. Teams have already played in Brazil, Australia and England this season with more to come later down the line in France and Spain. That’s not to say there isn’t still a desire to see teams from across the league overseas, but it appears as fans in the UK are beginning to demand more marquee matchups given the novelty has worn off. When the Philadelphia Eagles and the Jacksonville Jaguars face off next Sunday, it should feel like a completely different ball game. So to answer Shakespeare, perhaps you can have too much of a good thing, but at least, the weather was nice.

articles.body:
After finishing with just 63 rushing yards on 14 carries in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the New York Giants, Arizona Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love raised some eyebrows by uttering a word that young players typically avoid.

Love revealed to reporters after the game that his body felt "tired" as he continues to adjust to having his snaps managed to start his NFL career.

"My body sometimes is down," Love said. "Sometimes tired. So it's just managing those things. And coaches know that. This is probably gonna be the longest year of my life. I just want to manage that workload. So today just obviously making sure to keep an eye on managing me. But I didn't go out there hurt anything or anything like that. They're doing what they need to do to keep me up so that I can finish the season."

In his first four NFL games, Love has registered fewer than 15 carries three times and hasn't surpassed the 100-yard mark. He had career highs of 21 carries and 90 rushing yards in Week 3 against the San Francisco 49ers, but he failed to carry that momentum into Sunday's game against the Giants. He was seen on the sidelines having his ankle worked on by a trainer during the third quarter.

While Love downplayed any injury concerns, he admitted that he doesn't feel like the same version of himself he was last season at Notre Dame, though he made it clear that his frustration is with himself and not with the coaching staff.

"I'm really frustrated with myself because I just want to be good," Love told reporters . "I want to be 100 percent and I want to go out there and do what I need to do. Not saying I'm not 100 percent, but I'm not where I want to be. I'm not able to go out there and do spectacular plays every single time or stuff like that. So, just frustrated with myself, not with the coaches, but they're doing a great job of managing me."

Things could get a little easier for Love and the Cardinals in Week 5, as they will be facing a Detroit Lions team that is allowing 119.8 rushing yards per game and a league-worst 31.8 points per game. A big performance from the 2026 No. 3 pick could help Arizona snap its three-game skid.

But how can a Year 2 quarterback have Mahomes-level conviction after almost three wins and 18 losses - just two years - into the NFL?Cam Ward shows Patrick Mahomes level confidence amid Titans strugglesIn 2025, Cam Ward saw coaching battles between Brian Callahan and Mike McCoy. Callahan was fired after a 1-5 start. McCoy led the Tennessee Titans to a 3-14 season. Both head coaches were fired. The only constant? 2025 rookie quarterback Cameron Ward.What happens in 2026? The team brought in Robert Saleh from the San Francisco 49ers. Saleh was promoted from defensive coordinator. The only constant, other than their 2025 draft pick? A 0-4 start to the season.Despite this history repeating itself in the weirdest form possible, how has Cam Ward showcased himself? “We got three minutes left, [I’ll] walk out” is how he responds to reporters at the press conference after the winless record continued following the Baltimore Ravens defeat in Week 4.For someone as great as Patrick Mahomes, that kind of attitude makes sense, even though the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback has never given up on his down-to-earth, beyond-humble qualities.But to have that Mahomes-level of [expected, but never found] attitude after a 3-14 rookie year and a 0-4 start in his second year? It just shows how much Cam Ward values the game… and how much he values talking about it.Cam Ward’s confidence faces scrutiny without resultsAn X post referenced by MLFootball puts Cam Ward’s demeanor under the scrutiny microscope. It invites fans to compare the year 2 QB’s press conference presence with the supreme confidence associated with Patrick Mahomes.There is absolutely nothing wrong with projecting confidence. In fact, unfaltering confidence is required after four consecutive losses. But confidence without results can quickly start looking like arrogance.And this could lead to a growingly frustrated fan base. That’s the harsh reality that Cam Ward likely faces. Patrick Mahomes speaks with the authority of a superstar because of his elite performance. His gridiron stats and the Kansas City Chiefs’ Super Bowl wins have backed his authoritative confidence. Cam Ward may not have that luxury, just not yet.The 2025 draft pick could back his confidence if he turns it into wins. He still has so much to gain. He could come back with only wins. This could be his final four losses of the season.Also, Tennessee’s struggles cannot be placed entirely on Ward’s shoulders. But if he shows a Mahomes-like attitude, he may need stats to back it up.Mahomes is still killing it on the gridiron - he is 4-0. And Ward is 0-4. articles.title: Vrabel Trolls CJGJ in Viral Video After DB Says Patriots 'Didn't Do S--t Better Than' Bills in Win
articles.summary: New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel fired back at Buffalo Bills safety CJ Gardner-Johnson for his post-game comments after the Patriots' 29-26 victory on Sunday.
articles.body:
New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel fired back at Buffalo Bills safety CJ Gardner-Johnson for his post-game comments after the Patriots' 29-26 victory on Sunday.

After Gardner-Johnson declared that the Patriots "didn't do s--t better than us" and called wide receiver Efton Chism a "practice-squad player" who "made a hell of a play" with a go-ahead one-handed touchdown catch, Vrabel trolled the eight-year veteran during his radio appearance on Monday.

"For a guy that's been on eight teams in four years? I mean, I guess he knows the drill," Vrabel said with a laugh.

In fairness to Chism, the undrafted second-year pro has been a member of New England's 53-man roster since 2025 and was never on the practice squad. He's seeing more opportunities in the Patriots' offense this year while star wideout A.J. Brown recovers from an ankle sprain, and he made a highlight-reel catch when he snagged a touchdown pass from Drake Maye with under two minutes left in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game.

"We all believe he's one of the best quarterbacks in the league," Chism said of Maye, per Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer . "He makes plays each and every week, each and every day in practice. And so we just got to continue to be there for him. And any time he gives us an opportunity as receivers or as running backs or anyone, be there for him so he can build that confidence in himself, like we all know he has. He's an awesome player, an awesome captain and an awesome guy."

It was a much-needed victory for a Patriots team that was coming off an abysmal 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 3.

"I think it's just that no matter what's going on in previous weeks or what's the future, we're focused on it and we're continuing to build that identity," Chism said. "And it's not going to become something overnight. We're going to have to continue to finish, and have the effort to finish, and just be those guys out there that continue to play relentlessly."

Still, Gardner-Johnson wasn't impressed as he blasted Chism and the rest of the Patriots after the Bills had their three-game winning streak snapped.

"Listen, we're not going to get into no bulletin-board material," Gardner-Johnson told reporters . "An elevated guy made a helluva catch. Probably won't hear from him again. Respectfully. And I say that with a lot of confidence because… [Drake Maye] didn't put his confidence in his best player. He would've thrown it to [Romeo] Doubs or something. But they won the game. Whatever. They didn't do s--t better than us. We gotta play better. And they can mark that. We'll be back to see them again at the end of the year, so they can have that same energy. And they put up, what, 20-something points? They barely scored, they struggled all game. A practice-squad player made a hell of a play."

It's safe to say that Gardner-Johnson provided the bulletin-board material that New England will use when it faces Buffalo again in December. The AFC East rivals are among the top Super Bowl contenders in the conference, so it won't be a surprise to see even more fireworks in their next matchup.

articles.title: Latest on Pat Surtain II's 'Weird' Injury, Timeline to Return to Broncos Revealed in New NFL Rumors
articles.summary: Denver Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain II could miss multiple weeks due to the ankle injury he suffered in Sunday's 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
Denver Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain II could miss multiple weeks due to the ankle injury he suffered in Sunday's 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

Rapoport described the injury as "kind of a weird one" because the 2024 Defensive Player of the Year pulled up without contact and was favoring his right foot:

While the nature of the injury is unclear, Rapoport reported the Broncos have ruled out an Achilles-related issue.

The Ringer's Tom Pelissero initially reported Sunday night that Surtain's Achilles is "intact."

Surtain and the Broncos may have dodged a bullet. Still, his absence for multiple weeks would be a big blow for the defense.

Through Denver's first four games, he had 21 tackles and one pass breakup. Opposing quarterbacks have steered clear of him for the most part. He has been targeted just 14 times, allowing eight completions, according to Pro Football Reference .

Compounding matters for the Broncos, they watched their other starting cornerback, Riley Moss, leave Sunday with a rib injury.

Linebacker Alex Singleton praised the efforts of Kris Abrams-Draine and Jahdae Barron against the Niners.

"Young guys stepped up huge," he told reporters . " … Thankfully, they were both ready to play football."

This could present Barron, a 2025 first-round pick, with a springboard to showcase his skills in a larger role. He appeared in all 17 games last year but was on the field for just 30 percent of the team's defensive snaps.

Even if Barron settles in nicely, there's bound to be a drop between he and Surtain. And losing a defensive back who so effectively blankets opposing receivers could have a wider effect on the scheme of coordinator Vance Joseph.

articles.title: Week 5 Waiver Wire Pickups Highlighted by C.J. Stroud, Tank Bigsby, Keon Coleman
articles.summary: Working the fantasy football waiver wire can, at times, feel entirely optional.
articles.body:
Working the fantasy football waiver wire can, at times, feel entirely optional.

Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season probably isn't one of those times.

Not with the injury count perpetually increasing, and certainly not with the campaign's first bye week entering the equation.

You (almost assuredly) need some roster reinforcements, then, so let's help you find some with three waiver-wire targets available in 50-plus percent of leagues (per FantasyPros ).

Tank Bigsby, RB, Philadelphia Eagles (26% Rostered)

The Eagles, who were already down go-to wideout DeVonta Smith, lost star running back Saquon Barkley to a hamstring injury Sunday . The mere possibility that Barkley misses time should rank Tank Bigsby high on this week's list of priority targets.

When the Eagles lost Barkley on Sunday, they looked Bigsby's direction early and often.

The fourth-year back wound up receiving 14 carries and one target; Will Shipley, meanwhile, had six carries and a target. (Neither caught their lone target for whatever that's worth.) A Barkley-less backfield, then, should largely belong to Bigsby.

Now, Bigsby hasn't looked great so far (55 yards Sunday), but he did average 5.7 yards per carry last season and has a seven-score season on his resume (2024 with the Jacksonville Jaguars). The potential opportunity creates the interest here, but the fact he is talented enough to do something with it really solidifies his appeal.

Keon Coleman, WR, Buffalo Bills (8% Rostered)

The stars have admittedly failed to align so far for Keon Coleman, who joined the Bills as a second-round pick in 2024.

That said, there are reasons to believe they'll come together yet.

With DJ Moore struggling to shake a shoulder injury, Coleman has climbed up the Bills' pass-catching pecking order and done everything he can to keep that ascension going. On Sunday, he popped for six receptions on seven targets for 116 yards and a score. On the season, he has now collected 14 of the 16 passes sent his way.

His game log still shows volatility—he had one reception each in Weeks 1 and 3—but that combination of his efficiency and Moore's health could finally give Coleman stability and sustainability with his stats.

C.J. Stroud, QB, Houston Texans (43% Rostered)

It's been a rough-go for the winless Texans as a whole, but C.J. Stroud is showing he still capable of producing fantasy fireworks.

Especially if Nico Collins is on the field.

Sunday marked just the second time Stroud has played with his star receiver this season. Stroud went 21-of-31 in that contest for 347 yards and two touchdowns. During Collins' other outing this season (Week 1), Stroud threw for 274 yards and two touchdowns. For reference, Stroud's other two games have featured just 520 yards and one score combined.

Stroud has scored the 11th-most fantasy points on the season among quarterbacks, and he's only had his go-to target around for half of his games. If that pair gets more field time together moving forward, Stroud could emerge as a trustworthy weekly starter.

articles.title: 49ers' Dre Greenlaw Told Broncos' Sean Payton to 'Get the F--k Off the Field' in Exchange on Video
articles.summary: Dre Greenlaw seemingly had words for his former coach during Sunday's game between the San Francisco 49ers.
articles.body:
Dre Greenlaw seemingly had words for his former coach during Sunday's game between the San Francisco 49ers.

The veteran linebacker was released by the Broncos this offseason and appeared to say something to head coach Sean Payton during and after Sunday's meeting.

"I told him to get the f--k off the field," Greenlaw said of his postgame exchange, per Eric Branch of the San Francisco Chronicle . "That's it: 'Get the f--k off the field.'"

NFL investigating 2 referees for separate viral exchanges

Greenlaw also noted that he was motivated by "the disrespect," calling out Payton for not calling him to inform him about his release:

Those comments come after he discussed the matter with reporters in the locker room.

"I mean, I just haven't talked to him in months. Even since I was on the team," Greenlaw said. "It's just a lot."

Payton had nothing bad to say about Greenlaw after the game and said that he and the player are "all good."

"I think the world of him. I love everything about him," Payton said. "He plays with that emotion and so, all good."

Greenlaw ultimately got the last laugh over his head coach, as he and the Niners beat the Broncos 24-14 to improve to 4-0. Greenlaw led the team with 12 tackles, a season high for him thus far.

It's unclear what exactly went down between Greenlaw and Payton in Denver, but being released by a team always leaves some negative feelings. That much was evident on Sunday.

articles.title: Inside the remarkable comeback that has Patriots teammates calling Drake Maye unstoppable
articles.summary: Trailing by five with four minutes left, Drake Maye led a composed, methodical drive that left his Patriots locker room — and Highmark Stadium — in disbelief...
articles.body:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. – As the football soared in the air for a brief moment on Sunday, the noise level at Highmark Stadium was deafening. But in an instant, a hush fell over the crowd.

All it took was a perfectly placed pass to an undersized and relatively unknown receiver.

Right after Drake Maye completed a game-winning touchdown pass to Efton Chism III, Patriots left tackle Will Campbell turned to his quarterback.

"I said, 'You're the best in the [expletive] world,'" Campbell said. "And everybody in here believes in him and knows what he can do and bring to this team. And I think it showed today."

Over the first three weeks of the 2026 NFL season, there were many opinions about the Patriots quarterback. Maye entered Sunday's matchup in Buffalo as an underdog, who led the NFL in interceptions coming off a blowout loss.

Maye wasn't perfect on this sunny afternoon in Orchard Park, N.Y., but much like his teammates, he never lost faith. Considering how previous games went this season, it wouldn't have been a surprise to see the Patriots lose on Sunday.

Trailing by five points with 4:21 remaining, it looked more and more like the Patriots and their quarterback would come up short. Instead, a calm, cool and collected 24-year-old brought a level of poise to the Patriots huddle when they needed it the most.

Just when people thought Maye and the Patriots were collapsing, the quarterback and his teammates proved many wrong in this stunning 29-26 comeback win over the Bills. For those in the locker room, it wasn't a surprise to see Maye rise to the challenge.

"I never have lost any faith or confidence or anything in that guy," tight end Hunter Henry said. "He's a competitor. He just continues to go to work. He wants to get better. Even when things didn't go our way today, just kept fighting. Kept battling. That's what it's all about."

That's what it took for the Patriots to upset the Bills on Sunday.

Over the first three weeks, the Patriots offense operated at a concerningly low level. The group scored 10 points in Week 1, 13 in Week 2 and scored just 6 points in Week 3 in Jacksonville. The primary concerns were levied on Maye's shoulder.

The young quarterback led the NFL in interceptions to go with two fumbles.

On Sunday, the Patriots offense started fast, scoring 14 points in the first quarter, surpassing the totals from their previous three games. In that first half, however, a familiar issue popped up.

Maye was strip-sacked at 10:14 of the first quarter and then intercepted late in the second.

Had the quarterback followed the script from Seattle or Jacksonville, more turnovers would've followed in the second half. Instead, teammates say Maye gave them confidence when they needed it the most.

Following a Josh Allen touchdown pass, the Patriots trailed 26-21 with 4:21 remaining. Maye walked on the field with an elevated self-assurance.

"You just look him in the eyes and you just know it's time to go," center Jared Wilson said. "It's just us 11 in the huddle. We look each other in the eyes and, like, do it for the guy next to you. You ain't got to worry about your mistakes or whatever, because the next guy next to you got your back. Go out there, play carefree and win the game."

"Poise. He was very poised in that huddle," DeMario Douglas added. "Just watching him in that moment, man, some people panic. He was very poised and I'm proud of him."

With a hostile crowd losing their minds, Maye collected himself and his teammates. On the first play, he completed a 14-yard pass to Henry at the 41-yard line. Two plays later, he connected with Romeo Doubs for a 13-yard reception near midfield.

"Just calm, cool and ready to go," Henry said. " It's cool to see him thrive in that scenario."

"Poised, man.," Doubs added. "In moments like that, there's no reason to panic, especially with the ball in our hands."

Adding to the degree of difficulty, the Patriots offense was already playing without top receiver A.J. Brown and starting right guard Michael Onwenu when Mack Hollins suffered a calf injury in the first half. The veteran receiver left the game leading the team in receiving yards with 53.

After scoring 21 points, the Patriots punted in the next three drives with Hollins out. The injury situation forced the Patriots to play young receivers like Chism and Kyle Williams.

Williams noted that Maye's level of confidence in the huddle on the game-winning drive radiated throughout the group.

"A demon," Williams said of Maye. "He just came out there and conducted what he was supposed to do," Williams said. ""His energy was there, so we followed along with it. And when you got somebody that's in that groove, it's hard to stop him. And he was unstoppable."

After connecting with Doubs, Maye completed a 17-yard pass to Chism, setting the Patriots up at the 28-yard line. Three plays later, on third down, Maye threw a perfectly placed 23-yard pass to Chism, who corralled the ball with one arm.

The Bills still had a chance but after a Craig Woodson interception, Maye threw a 12-yard pass to Henry on third-and-10 allowing the Patriots to run out the clock.

"One thing about Drake is he's always composed," right tackle Morgan Moses said. "Nothing gets too big and he never gets too low. When you have a guy like that under center, you're in good hands."

An hour after the game ended, the Patriots were loud inside the visitors locker room. Maye was all smiles. Teammates and coaches stopped by his locker one after another to revel in the upset. It wasn't too long ago people thought this Patriots season might be lost.

Following the win, Mike Vrabel greeted players in the locker room with a simple message: "We're not dead."

"If you listen to the outsiders, it's like a catastrophe. We're burning, everything's terrible," cornerback Carlton Davis said. "But inside this locker room, we always kept the faith and we always knew what we could do."

Davis then pointed to Maye, calling him one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL. With the pressure on, the Patriots quarterback didn't flinch. His teammates soon followed.

"He's very poised. He's very calm, very intentional. I don't think he flinches ever," Campbell said. "I think that's something that helps him so much. He never is up and down, riding the emotional roller coaster of the ups and downs of the game. He's just even-keeled, looking to make the next play."

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr. says Giants ‘got me’ after release from second stint in New York
articles.summary: Beckham says he returned to New York on a veteran-minimum deal expecting to contribute, but received just one target across
articles.body:
Beckham says he returned to New York on a veteran-minimum deal expecting to contribute, but received just one target across three games.

Odell Beckham Jr. has broken his silence after the New York Giants released him just three games into his second stint with the team. He says he now believes the organization benefited from the attention surrounding his return while he received little opportunity to contribute on the field.

Beckham made the comments on Instagram while responding to a post accusing the Giants of using his return as a publicity move. As reported by Yahoo Sports, he appeared to agree with that assessment, writing that "they got me" and "they won." Beckham, 33, returned to the franchise that selected him 12th overall in the 2014 NFL Draft after sitting out the 2025 season.

He made New York's initial 53-man roster after accepting a veteran-minimum contract, but his role quickly became limited. He played roughly 20 offensive snaps across three games and received only one target, which fell incomplete. Reflecting on the decision to return, Beckham wrote that he came to New York "HUMBLY", accepted the veteran minimum and believed he had earned his place on the roster. He then added, "I shoulda known better."

The veteran receiver also made clear that he does not view the Giants release as proof that his NFL career should be over. "I coulda really been playing this year somewhere and making a impact," Beckham wrote. His comments suggest that he believes returning to New York may have cost him an opportunity elsewhere, although that remains his personal assessment rather than an established fact.

The Giants released Beckham on Sept. 29 after three games. He finished his brief comeback without a reception. Giants head coach John Harbaugh has offered a different explanation for the decision. Harbaugh said the organization simply was not getting enough production from Beckham's roster spot and could not find a way to get him sufficiently involved in the offense.

"It just wasn't working for us," Harbaugh said, adding that the decision was about what the team needed from its roster rather than Beckham's popularity or the attention surrounding his return. The Giants subsequently made roster moves that included adding return specialist Braxton Berrios, further changing the team's personnel needs.

articles.title: Vikings’ bizarre 4-0 start is powered by defense and a whole lot of field goals
articles.summary: How the heck are the Vikings 4-0 with an offense this lifeless?
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings are 4-0, standing today as one of the three undefeated teams left in the National Football League.

And while you never apologize for winning games in the NFL, how the Vikings have maintained this status is one of the quirkiest aspects of the early 2026 season.

While the other two teams are led by potent offenses with one of the league's best rushing attacks (the Kansas City Chiefs) and one of the league's best passing games (the San Francisco 49ers), the Vikings are winning largely with their defense.

In fact, almost solely with their defense.

We can start with Sunday's 15-10 win over the Miami Dolphins. While Minnesota outgained Miami 336 to 198, and racked up 20 first downs compared to just eight for the Dolphins, all 15 points for the Vikings came off the right foot of kicker Will Reichard.

Five field goals, zero touchdowns, for Minnesota on Sunday.

Zooming out for a moment, this is now the second game this season where the Vikings did not score an offensive touchdown, and every point came from their kicker. In Minnesota's Week 2 win over the Chicago Bears, the Vikings used three field goals from Reichard to win by a final score of 9-3.

And Sunday's final score of 15-10 saw the Vikings join a rather small list.

According to Kevin Seifert of ESPN, Minnesota is just the third team in NFL history to begin the year 4-0 despite failing to score a touchdown in multiple games. The other two teams on that list? The 1922 Chicago Cardinals … and the 1923 Chicago Cardinals:

As discovered by Bryan Knowles from FTN, the Vikings — with just seven touchdowns this season — have scored the fewest touchdowns from a team that started 4-0 since the 2003 Carolina Panthers, and the tenth-fewest touchdowns from a 4-0 team in league history:

And when you break down Minnesota's scoring this year, while Reichard is by far the Vikings' leading scorer with 42 points this year, the entire Minnesota offense has combined to score 44 points, just two more than the kicker:

As found by Pro Football Reference, Reichard's 42 points leads the NFL through four weeks.

A final note on Minnesota's offense, through the prism of Expected Points Added. Looking at every NFL offense through four weeks — noting that the New Orleans Saints and the Atlanta Falcons have yet to play — note where the Vikings offense is on this graphic from RBSDM , which examines EPA/Rush and EPA/Pass:

Minnesota is below league average in both categories, in a cluster of teams that includes the Philadelphia Eagles, the Los Angeles Chargers, and the Dolphins.

Those other three teams have a combined 2-10 record.

So exactly how are the Vikings winning? It does start with the defense. Brian Flores' unit is almost off the chart when you look at EPA allowed against both the run and the pass this season, again from RBSDM:

And you can pick almost any other defensive category, and the Vikings are at or near the top of the league. Minnesota has held opposing passers to an Adjusted Net Yards per Attempt of just 4.5 (third-best in the league) during a season where the league average ANY/A for NFL quarterbacks is 6.3. For reference, Jacoby Brissett has an ANY/A of 4.5, and Jameis Winston checks in at 4.3.

The Vikings have held opposing offenses to just 94.5 yards per game on the ground (seventh-best in the NFL) and 194.8 yards per game in the air, again seventh-best in the NFL.

But where Minnesota's defense really sets itself apart is in conversions against , and in scoring allowed. The Vikings have allowed third-down conversions on just 22.6% of chances this season (the best mark in the league), and teams have scored a touchdown when reaching the end zone on just 18.2% of chances this season (again the best mark in the league from any defense). And Minnesota has allowed just 12.8 points per game this season, topping that category among NFL defenses.

Now, some context. Minnesota's four wins have come against the Green Bay Packers, the Bears, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and now the Dolphins. Both the Dolphins and the Buccaneers have yet to win a game, the victory over Chicago came on a wet and dreary day in the Windy City, and the Packers' offensive line has been underwhelming, to say the least.

So these numbers may change as the Vikings play some better offenses, like the Buffalo Bills in Week 9 or the San Francisco 49ers in Week 11.

Returning to the offense for a final moment, if there is one thing Minnesota is doing right, it is this: The Vikings are taking care of the football. Minnesota has turned the ball over just twice this season, both on interceptions, and that turnover percentage of just 4.5% is seventh-best in the league.

With a defense like theirs, the old adage of "end every drive with a kick" remains true.

Through four weeks, this Vikings team remains undefeated.

Even if the recipe to get there is rather quirky.

articles.title: Packers By The Numbers: Stats from the Week 4 win over the Bucs
articles.summary: Digging into some numbers on the Packers’ Week 4 victory over the Bucs
articles.body:
As we do every week in this space, we're looking at some stats from the Green Bay Packers game, courtesy of SumerSports .

Last week saw the Packers needing to lean heavy into 11 personnel and the passing game, due to getting behind early and also lacking any ability to run. This week saw them with a little more balance, both in terms of personnel usage and in run/pass ratio. This week, the Packers were in 11 personnel (1 RB, 1 TE, 3 WR) on just 47.3% of their snaps (down from 81% last week). They were in 12 personnel on 23.6% and 13 personnel on 29.1% of their snaps.

That 13 personnel rate (1 RB, 3 TE, 1 WR) was their highest usage of that personnel package this year, and it was also their best passing package. When operating out of 13 personnel, Jordan Love was 5/5 for 76 yards for an EPA per Play of +1.04 (basically, they generated a little more than 1 point every time they passed out of this grouping). They had a 100% Success Rate when passing out of 13 personnel. It was also their best running group (11 attempts, 52 yards, -0.09 EPA per Play). I'm excited to dig into the film on that and see what they were doing when in that personnel group.

On the run/pass ratio, the Packers passed 56.4% of the time and ran 43.6% of the time. That's a far cry from the 85.7% pass rate we saw against the Falcons. The pass game (+0.14 EPA per Play) far outperformed the run game (-0.35). While an 85.7% pass rate is a bit extreme, I'd certainly like to see the pass rate be a little closer to 65% rather than 55%.

Love was still getting the ball out quickly (he averaged 2.17 seconds to throw, a full 0.5 seconds below the NFL average), with an EPA per Play of +0.14. That's far and away his best passing performance of the year. Before this, his best performance was in the Vikings game in Week 1, where he posted an EPA per Play of -0.02.

For the first time this year, Love took 0 sacks. There were some plays he'd like to have back and there were (once again) a couple drops, but this is the most competent the Packers offense has looked all year.

Love also looked good against the blitz. That's been an issue all year (mainly because, against the line through the first 3 weeks, a blitz meant an automatic pressure), but Love did well this week. Against the blitz, he was 7/9 for 62 yards (+0.14 EPA per Play).

It was also an encouraging performance from Tucker Kraft. He caught 6 of his 7 targets for 42 yards and a TD, good for +0.79 EPA per Reception. He had an ADOT (Average Depth of Target) of 0.57 yards and he averaged 6.83 yards after the catch. He wasn't asked to stretch the field very much (his targets were on Hitches and Quick Outs), but when he got the ball in his hands he got upfield and was looking to make something happen. He still doesn't look like the Tucker Kraft we were used to seeing last season, but this was the first time all year we really got a good glimpse of that guy. Overall, Kraft had a 22.6% target share. He was a heavy target in the Red Zone (42.9% target share) and saw a decent amount of looks on early downs (27.3% early down target share).

Kraft also had an EPA per Play of +1.93 on rush attempts, thanks to his successful 4th down sneak.

Here's what the running game numbers looked like from Gap Outcomes, by running back.

Brooks is their most limited runner in terms of burst/wiggle, but, if the line can block it up, he's been their most effective because he can read his blocks and hit the hole.

Let's take a quick look at the guards before moving to the other side of the ball. Last week, Jacob Monk (LG) allowed 8.3% pressure rate, with a 22.2% pressure rate against blitz, 5.3% pressure rate vs stunts. On the other side, Jager Burton (RG) allowed an 18.2 pressure rate, with an 11.1% pressure rate against the blitz and 20.8% vs stunts.

This week, we had Travis Glover (RG) giving up a 3.3% pressure rate, 0% rate against the blitz, 0% against stunts. New Packer Laken Tomlinson gave up a 3.3% pressure rate, 11.1% against the blitz, 0% against stunts.

I'm not going to sit here and proclaim that the interior of the line has been fixed, but, against a pretty good Tampa Bay front, Glover and Tomlinson performed well.

The Packers lived in Nickel in this game, posting a 90.2% Nickel rate (30.38% above the NFL average). That seems high, until you look and see they were just matching the Bucs' personnel. The Bucs were in 11 personnel on 90.2% of their snaps. When the Bucs brought out a 3rd WR, the Packers were matching in Nickel.

The Packers defense was zone heavy, but not quite as much as they had been. They played Man Coverage on 39.4% of their snaps, their highest rate of the year (their previous high was 13.3% against the Vikings). The Man snaps were primarily Cover 1 (man-to-man across the board, with a single-high safety), but they also ran 2 snaps of Cover 0 (all-out blitz with man coverage).

This was also the highest blitz rate the Packers had all year. They blitzed the Bucs on 47.22% of their snaps, 17.09% above NFL average. Their previous high was 34.69% against the Jets. The defense has been a bit uneven at times (which is putting it a bit nicely), but I have been quite happy with Gannon's blitz approach. Coming into the year, Gannon was known as a defensive coordinator who didn't blitz very often. This year, he has dialed it up more than we've seen in his career, and has leaned heavier into the blitz depending on the gameplan. Seeing that type of flexibility in attack has been really fun.

Lukas Van Ness had a nice performance, but not quite as impactful as we had been seeing. He notched 2 solo tackles, 2 assisted tackles and 0 tackles for loss. I'd like to see his pressure rate higher (his 8.7% pressure rate was 3.23% below NFL average), but that was due to a quick release and screen-heavy plan from the Bucs. His Average Time to Pressure was 2.36 seconds, right around NFL average.

articles.title: CBS sideline reporter Aditi Kinkhabwala says Trey McBride said ‘please’ before official’s profane outburst
articles.summary: By one eyewitness’s account, Trey McBride was the most polite person in his argument with an NFL official on Sunday. That’s according to CBS sideline reporte...
articles.body:
By one eyewitness's account, Trey McBride was the most polite person in his argument with an NFL official on Sunday.

That's according to CBS sideline reporter Aditi Kinkhabwala, who was standing within earshot when line judge Jeff Seeman seemingly lost his temper with the Cardinals' star tight end in the fourth quarter of Sunday's loss to the Giants.

"I was standing right there," she wrote. "What's wild is that it all started with Trey McBride saying 'please' when pleading his case for a PI flag. He was heated for sure, but I never heard a curse from him. The harshest he got was, 'You're ruining the game.'"

Seeman's response was far less restrained, as a CBS camera caught the official appearing to shout "f*ck you" at McBride twice, prompting the Cardinals tight end to turn around, point directly at the camera that had captured the outburst, and burst out laughing at the realization that the whole thing was now on tape.

By Sunday night, the NFL had opened a review. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the league was reviewing the exchange , and a spokesperson confirmed as much to Pro Football Talk shortly after NFLPA executive director JC Tretter posted the damning footage and demanded the league hold Seeman accountable.

Week 4 had already delivered more than its share of colorful, R-rated audio before Seeman joined the chorus. Prime Video's microphones caught Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy cursing at each other during Thursday night's Steelers-Browns game, while Fox picked up Jalen Hurts excoriating one of his receivers . But those outbursts came from players and coaches caught up in the emotion of a game, while Sunday's came from the one man on the field who's paid to stay above it.

The NFL has not said when its review will conclude or what discipline Seeman could face.

articles.title: 'I'm a dog,' Cowboys’ CB Porter was beyond impressive in Week 4 debut
articles.summary: They can't all be highlight reels. How Joey Porter Jr's debut with the Dallas Cowboys was perfectly uneventful in Week 4
articles.body:
Sometimes making a big splash is a bad thing. Olympic diving, cat burglary, bomb defusal, and NFL cornerbacking, all experience moments where the less splash, the better. Joey Porter Jr.'s NFL debut constitutes a moment of a little splash being a big win.

When the Dallas Cowboys traded for Porter on September 30, they weren't quite sure when he'd be contributing. Porter hadn't played this season amidst a contract dispute wrapped up in a back injury. He was in shape but maybe not game shape.

"That's why I wasn't really out there too much," Porter said via DallasCowboys.com .

With their Week 5 matchup against the Houston Texans just four days away, asking him to hit the field immediately seemed more than a little ambitious. Yet hit the ground running is exactly what Porter did this week, and the results were beautifully uneventful.

Based on early tracking by Sumer Sports , Porter played 16 coverage snaps against the Texans on Sunday. Of those snaps he was targeted zero times, allowed zero receptions, for zero yards and zero touchdowns. It was splashless in all the right ways.

Next Gen Stats registered one target but zero success for Houston on that target, so the results were ultimately the same. PFF tracked 20 coverage snaps and came away with the same row of zeros. The All-22 will be the ultimate say but the results won't change; Porter locked things down.

"I'm a dog at the end of the day, and I want to be out there with the guys," Porter said. "So I have to prove why they got me here, and I feel like I did that today."

In 2026, the Cowboys secondary has been making splashes for all the wrong reasons. They came into Week 4 ranked No. 31 in EPA/dropback allowed. Their revolving door of personnel made things inconsistent and difficult to build on. Getting a player of Porter's quality into the fold as soon as possible was important for Dallas, so get him into the fold they did.

Porter didn't look like a player wanting to ease into things. He was looking for Nico Collins early and occasionally got what he was asking for. While he wasn't put to the test, he put up some good film, allowing very little separation and displaying inspiring fundamentals along the way. There was a reason he was avoided.

It finally looks like the Cowboys have a real one at the cornerback position. With any luck the return of Cobie Durant will help solidify a unit that no longer needs someone like Reddy Steward taking double-digit snaps in the slot.

The Cowboys' defense is far from a good thing, but things are looking brighter with Porter now donning the star. Porter didn't have a splashy debut and that's a-okay for the Cowboys.

articles.title: NFL Monday Night Football preview: Saints and Falcons renew one of NFL's best rivalries
articles.summary: The winner of Monday night's game will be tied for first place in the NFC South.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons and New Orleans Saints saw their seasons take much different turns in Week 3.

The Falcons started the season 0-2 but got quarterback Michael Penix Jr. back in the lineup and looked like a different team, blowing out the Packers 35-14. Meanwhile, a Saints team that was coming off a dramatic win at Baltimore to improve to 1-1 lost a fourth-quarter lead to the Raiders and lost 35-27.

That sets up a matchup between two 1-2 teams that still have plenty of hope in a once again mediocre NFC South. The winner on Monday night will be 2-2 and tied with the Carolina Panthers for first place.

There's always a little extra on the line between the Saints and the Falcons, which is one of the NFL's most heated rivalries. And Monday night is being celebrated as the 20th anniversary of the "rebirth" at the Superdome, the Saints' return to their home stadium after Hurricane Katrina devastated New Orleans. That game is remembered best for Steve Gleason's blocked punt that led to a touchdown, and Gleason will be honored at the game Monday night. There will be a little more emotion in the New Orleans crowd than usual, and it's always high for a Falcons game.

But these two teams have more than history and a rivalry at stake. One will be 2-2 and tied for first place in the division. The other falls to 1-3, which is a tough hole to be in regardless of the division you play in.

The Falcons' season outlook completely changed when Penix returned to the lineup. He had been out while getting back to 100% from ACL surgery. Atlanta put up 498 yards in his return last week. Drake London in particular came alive with nine catches and 194 yards. The Falcons can ignore the first two losses of the season, with third- and fourth-string quarterbacks, and focus on a new season with Penix.

The Saints were the hottest team in the NFC South over the second half of last season and it looked like that carried over to this season. The 24-17 comeback win at the Ravens in Week 2 was impressive. Saints quarterback Tyler Shough is off to a hot start in his second season. But then came a disappointing Raiders loss, in which New Orleans turned it over four times in the fourth quarter, and the prospect of falling to 1-3 with a loss on Monday night.

There's a lot of history between these two franchises. The rivalry aside, this game is huge for both teams early this season.

There is nowhere near the pressure on this season's Saints for Monday night's game as there was on the 2006 Saints to win in the first game back in the Superdome against the Falcons. But there still is pressure on New Orleans. They had a good start to the season, coming a failed 2-point conversion from starting 2-0 at the Lions and Ravens. A home loss to the Raiders last week turned what looked like a pretty good start to the season into a 1-2 record. The Falcons have plenty on the line too. They don't want to lose the momentum gained from Michael Penix Jr.'s return to the lineup. But the Saints dropping a second straight home game to fall to 1-3 would be a bigger step back.

London is one of the NFL's best receivers when he has a competent quarterback. Through two weeks, with Cooper Rush and briefly rookie Jack Strand at quarterback, London had six catches for 80 yards. He was no factor in Atlanta's 0-2 start and nobody blamed him. Then came Week 3, and a 194-yard outburst with Michael Penix Jr. back. Penix has always liked peppering London with targets, going back to Penix's rookie season. London had 10 targets against the Packers and should come close to that on Monday night. The Saints haven't allowed more than 227 passing yards in a game this season, but that will be tested.

In a wide-open NFC South, this is an important early-season game for both teams. The betting public is backing the Saints, but we've seen the line drop from New Orleans -2.5 to -1.5 in what should be an electric environment. There are injuries aplenty, and with two young QBs in Tyler Shough and Michael Penix Jr. going at it, I'm looking at the over 47.5. Check to see if Falcons LB Divine Deablo can go — as Atlanta's D will be really shorthanded if he can't play.

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

Fantasy football storylines, by Scott Pianowski

We hope you're enjoying your subscription to the Atlanta Falcons Season Ticket (Week 2 of 3). Here are three fantasy themes to consider as you watch the Falcons and Saints wrap up Week 4.

1. What does the New Orleans backfield look like without Travis Etienne? A hamstring injury pushed Etienne to injured reserve this week, making an opportunity for Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller. Kamara has been stuck in a 2.8 YPC rut through his two games, with Miller only modestly better (3.4 YPC, and a higher success rate ). Both backs have seen limited receiving work, but that could change with Etienne hurt.

2. Can the Falcons find a third pitch on offense? Bijan Robinson can be Superman against anyone and obviously Drake London and Michael Penix have strong chemistry. But so far in Penix's career, he's been unable to click with TE Kyle Pitts . It will also be interesting to see how much Brian Robinson plays — Atlanta's No. 2 back has 30 carries over three games.

3. Will Juwan Johnson keep rolling? Johnson has a solid TE7, TE13, TE5 start to the year, poised for a strong return on his summer ADP. The Atlanta seam coverage has been leaky, allowing the eighth-most points to tight ends entering Week 4. Chris Olave is obviously the first read in the New Orleans passing game, but Johnson could stabilize as the second option.

articles.title: Joe Burrow Says 'This Isn't Armageddon' After Bengals' Loss to Jaguars amid Chase, Higgins Injuries
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is trying to remain even-keeled after a costly 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is trying to remain even-keeled after a costly 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday.

Beyond the fact Cincinnati dropped to 2-2 on the season, wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase suffered a concussion and Tee Higgins picked up an adductor injury.

"We had our opportunities in the last two weeks, but this isn't Armageddon or anything," Burrow told reporters . "We're still in a great spot [and] feel really good about our team."

New NFL contenders starting to emerge after Week 4

NFL investigating 2 referees for separate viral exchanges

The three-time Pro Bowler added the Bengals are "very confident" and noted it's still early into the season.

"We're 2-2, but nobody wins a championship after Week 4," he said.

Strong starts haven't been a feature of Burrow era in Cincinnati, and the Bengals have overcome them in the past. The team was 3-2 to open 2021 and eventually reached the Super Bowl. The following season, it went from a 2-3 record to the AFC title game.

The 0-4 Miami Dolphins are next on the schedule for the Bengals, and their Week 6 bye couldn't be better timed within the context of Chase and Higgins' injuries.

There were some concerning signs from Sunday's contest, namely the lack of offensive balance. Chase Brown ran for 10 yards on nine carries, while Burrow attempted 54 passes. The defense also allowed six yards per play to the Jags offense.

On the whole, the Bengals have at least shown enough that leads you to believe they can snap their three-year playoff drought. And nobody sets the tone inside the locker room more than Burrow. His outward confidence should rub off on his teammates.
